item.title: The Everything Bubble is back and bigger than ever
item.description: Five years ago, financial speculation was running amok. Then interest rates rose and stocks entered a short-lived bear market. Now the same warnings are flashing again: excess liquidity, high leverage, and exuberant retail investors. The next correction could be more dramatic.
item.dc:creator: Edward Chancellor
item.content:encoded: Five years ago, financial speculation was running amok. This was the heyday of meme stocks, special purpose acquisition companies (SPACs), non-fungible tokens and dubious cryptocurrencies such as Dogecoin. In the summer of 2021 Richard Bernstein, the former Merrill Lynch quantitative strategist turned portfolio manager, put out a note listing five factors which pointed to the existence of a stock market bubble. Within months US equities had peaked and over the following year entered bear market territory. Now the so-called “Everything Bubble” has returned with a vengeance. This time the downside risks appear much greater. Bernstein, who is now global head of macro at the investment firm Janus Henderson, listed increased liquidity as the first bubble factor. Back in 2021, the US money supply was surging after the Federal Reserve’s massive pandemic-induced bond-buying schemes. That excess cash spilled over into the stock market. The US central bank’s balance sheet is no longer exploding. Still, says Bernstein, financial conditions today remain remarkably easy. The Chicago Fed’s index which tracks the metric has trended downwards since late 2022 but remains slightly above its 2021 trough. Increased leverage was a second factor. In 2021 Bernstein pointed out that many retail investors (including 80% of investors who are members of Gen Z) were borrowing to buy stocks. Speculators were also using single stock options to boost returns. There’s even more leverage around today. Margin debt has been growing faster than mortgage and credit card debt, says Bernstein, and now stands at record levels both in dollar terms and relative to GDP. Zero-day to expiry options account for around half of the total turnover of US stock options. Hedge fund leverage is also at an all-time high. In early 2021, the over-leveraged Archegos Capital Management blew up. This summer, Situational Awareness, which had borrowed heavily to buy AI-related stocks, ran into trouble. The hedge fund, run by the former OpenAI employee Leopold Aschenbrenner, managed to avoid Archegos’ fate after Citadel Securities stepped in to acquire the bulk of its publicly listed securities. Other popular sources of speculative borrowing include leveraged single-stock exchange traded funds (ETFs). Defiance ETF, an asset management firm, is even planning to launch ETFs for popular stocks such as software firm Palantir Technologies (PLTR.O) and chip giant Nvidia (NVDA.O) that re-leverage every hour. The Chicago Mercantile Exchange this summer launched single-stock perpetual futures, or “perps”. Great investment bubbles often involve a rapid increase in the number of speculators, enticed into the market by opportunistic financial operators. Bernstein listed the democratisation of the market as a third bubble factor. Back in 2021 Robinhood Markets (HOOD.O) , the app-based broker, was the preferred platform for the crowd which rushed headlong into meme stocks and SPACs they discussed on Reddit’s WallStreetBets message board. Robinhood, whose app bore a passing resemblance to an electronic fruit machine, provided commission-free trading and cheap margin loans. Prior to its July 2021 IPO, Robinhood reported 18 million “funded accounts.” Since then it has added a further 10 million customers. Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev still extols his firm’s democratising mission: “Our product velocity is focused on one goal: making everyone an owner,” he said in July. In this case “product velocity” refers to the extension of Robinhood’s services from trading in shares, fractional shares and cryptocurrencies to making markets in tokenised equities (securities linked both to unlisted private companies such as OpenAI and publicly traded meme stocks like AMC Entertainment (AMC.N) ), and prediction markets. Prediction markets, which allow users to trade coin-flip contracts for a broad array of events, have taken off. Robinhood’s revenue from “event contracts” now [USN:L6N45813E TEXT:"exceeds its crypto business"]. The time-honoured distinction between investment, speculation and outright gambling is collapsing. Kalshi, which partners with Robinhood, recently applied for permission to issue “perps”. As Bernstein observes, “when people confuse the financial markets with the prediction markets something has gone really wrong.” The fourth factor signalling a market bubble is increased new issues. Five years ago, the amount raised by new companies listing on US exchanges reached an all-time high. Tech SPACs - among them Virgin Galactic (SPCE.N) , which offered space tourism, electric truck maker Nikola and battery developer QuantumScape (QS.O) - were all the rage. Nikola has since filed for bankruptcy while the share prices of Virgin Galactic and QuantumScape are down more than 95% from their peak. Today, the IPO market is even hotter. In June, Elon Musk’s SpaceX (SPCX.O) – arguably the greatest meme stock in history – raised a record $75 billion. AI leader Anthropic is [USN:L6N45F0XJ TEXT:"preparing a "][USN:L6N45F0XJ TEXT:"listing"] at a mooted $2 trillion valuation. Even SPACs are making a comeback. Bernstein’s fifth and final bubble factor was increased turnover. At the time, US stock market trading volume was running around 25% above its long-term average. This year, equities trading is even more frenetic. In January, the average daily US stock turnover exceeded $1 trillion for the first time. This summer, retail equities turnover was close to twice its average level since the turn of the decade, according to Citadel Securities. Volume on the Nasdaq market is also at record levels. The Everything Bubble proved vulnerable to the end of the zero-interest rate era that arrived in 2022. Today, interest rates and bond yields have returned to more normal levels. In other respects, though, the current bubble looks much more dangerous. The US stock market today is even more concentrated in a handful of giant companies and increasingly exposed to a single theme: AI. Even as OpenAI and Anthropic continue to burn cash, AI investment is driving corporate earnings. Much of the investment is financed with debt. Former Morgan Stanley strategist David Roche points out that total on- and off-balance sheet debt for US tech giants and AI labs exceeds $3 trillion. Circular financing among the leading AI players depends critically on expectations of continuously accelerating revenue growth, so that that even the slightest slowdown risks undermining the whole edifice. Prudent investors should be preparing not for a rerun of the short-lived 2022 bear market but something far more dramatic. Follow @Breakingviews on X

item.title: Lula holds lead over Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of Brazil election, Datafolha poll shows
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has maintained a two-percentage-point lead over Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, his main challenger, in a potential runoff ahead of October's election, a Datafolha poll showed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has maintained a two-percentage-point lead over Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, his main challenger, in a potential runoff ahead of October's election, a Datafolha poll showed on Thursday. In a simulated runoff, Lula would receive 47% of vote compared with 45% for Bolsonaro. A [USN:L1N459120 TEXT:"previous Datafolha poll"] last week had Lula leading Bolsonaro by 46% to 44%.

item.title: Ares fund withdrawal requests decline as private credit redemptions ease
item.description: Withdrawal requests at Ares Management's flagship private credit fund eased slightly in its third-quarter tender offer, a regulatory filing showed on Thursday, reflecting a broader cooldown in redemptions across the sector.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Withdrawal requests at Ares Management's (ARES.N) flagship private credit fund eased slightly in its third-quarter tender offer, a regulatory filing showed on Thursday, reflecting a broader cooldown in redemptions across the sector. Investors in the $22.7 billion Ares Strategic Income Fund (ASIF) sought to redeem 13.1% of shares in the third quarter, down from 14.4% in the previous quarter. The fund limited withdrawals to 5% of shares, the customary threshold for such vehicles. Wealthy individuals have pulled money from non-traded private credit funds in recent months amid concerns about lending standards and whether software companies that have borrowed heavily from direct lenders will weather AI disruption. But redemption pressures at major non-traded private credit funds are showing signs of easing as asset managers clear backlogs of withdrawal requests and investor sentiment rebounds from recent turbulence. Earlier this month, [USN:L4N4530XC TEXT:"BlackRock"] (BLK.N) and [USN:L4N45E1DG TEXT:"Apollo"] (APO.N) also reported a decline in redemption requests at their private credit funds. "Redemption demand is easing across most reporting funds, but at several of the largest, requests remain backlogged and persisting. It is too soon to conclude that the broader market has turned a corner, but the direction is encouraging," said Kevin Gannon, chairman and CEO of Stanger, which tracks so-called alternative assets. The Ares fund said much of the redemption pressure came from investors submitting repeat requests, adding that net new withdrawal demands amounted to 3% of net asset value. Major private credit funds have enforced the customary 5% limit on redemptions this year, keeping withdrawal requests elevated as investors resubmit unfulfilled requests in subsequent tender offers. "An investor who first submitted a repurchase request in Q1 2026 and has continued to resubmit any unfulfilled portion of that request in Q2 and Q3 is expected to have received nearly 80% of its originally requested capital," ASIF said. For these investors, the fund expects to mostly satisfy unfulfilled requests by year-end, assuming withdrawal requests remain in line with the third quarter. ASIF Class I shares have generated a 9.97% annualized total return since inception, representing a 161-basis-point premium to broadly syndicated bank loans. Data from Blue Owl (OWL.N) funds is expected in the coming weeks.

item.title: Trump tells countries to quit ICC. Few follow his lead
item.description: President Donald Trump urged countries to leave the International Criminal Court immediately, calling it "evil" and "a rogue institution," but only Naoero, a tiny Pacific island nation formerly known as Nauru, has followed suit during the UN General Assembly this week.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump urged countries to leave the International Criminal Court immediately, calling it "evil" and "a rogue institution," but only Naoero, a tiny Pacific island nation formerly known as Nauru, has followed suit during the UN General Assembly this week. Trump's appeal on Tuesday capped an escalating US campaign against the Hague-based court, which Washington says oversteps its authority by claiming jurisdiction over citizens of countries, including the United States and Israel, that have not ratified its founding treaty known as the Rome Statute. While a handful of countries have moved to leave the ICC, many governments, particularly in Europe, have rallied to defend it as a cornerstone of international justice. Parties to the statute include 125 countries. The US has imposed financial sanctions and visa bans on court staff, and officials have prepared [USN:FWN45A0PH TEXT:"sanctions"] that could undercut the court's [USN:L6N45D0HW TEXT:"ability to operate"], sources familiar with the matter said. 'DISMANTLE THE ICC' In July, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio launched a diplomatic push to "dismantle the ICC — brick by brick, if necessary," claiming the court posed a threat to American service members and those carrying out Trump's deportations of migrants and strikes on alleged drug trafficking boats. Trump has said the campaign is aimed at protecting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, against whom the ICC issued arrest warrants in 2024 alongside his then-defense minister and a Hamas military commander over the Gaza war. Since Rubio announced the campaign, Venezuela and Chad have announced plans to withdraw from the court. Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger announced their exits the previous year, denouncing the court as an instrument of "neocolonial repression." Naoero President David Adeang said in his speech to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday he would formally withdraw his country from the Rome Statute due to the ICC’s “increasing irrelevance.” "Naoero joins a growing number of nations standing up for their sovereignty against the ICC’s illegitimate overreach,” US Assistant Secretary for East Asian and Pacific Affairs Michael DeSombre said on X after meeting the island nation's deputy foreign minister. DEFENDING THE COURT The European Union rallied behind the Netherlands-based court and officials have discussed drawing up a blocking statute in response to the potential US sanctions. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters this week the bloc had options to defend the court. "We have the tools in our toolbox when it gets really serious, how to defend ICC, and here (at the UN) we are rallying countries behind supporting the ICC functioning and the accountability part because it's not only a European issue; it's much broader than that,” she said. Tomoko Akane, the ICC president already under US sanctions , is a Japanese national. Japan's government called the proposed sanctions "very unfortunate" and dispatched an official to The Hague to discuss how it could support her. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi noted Japan’s support for the ICC in her address to the General Assembly on Tuesday. “Since the end of the Second World War, Japan, as a peace-loving nation, has attached great importance to the rule of law in the settlement of any disputes,” Takaichi said. Brian Finucane, a senior adviser at the International Crisis Group, said many countries remain invested in the ICC's mission of accountability, limiting the impact of Washington's campaign against the court. He noted that Russian President Vladimir Putin targeted the ICC after it issued a warrant for his arrest. “The Trump administration has managed to align itself with Putin in terms of, you know, imposing targeting ICC personnel with sanctions, and of course, Putin would also benefit from the destruction of the court,” Finucane said.

item.title: MGM discusses bid for Barry Diller's People Inc, WSJ reports
item.description: MGM Resorts International is discussing making a bid to purchase Barry Diller’s People Inc , the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, a day after People Inc withdrew its proposal to buy MGM Resorts.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: MGM Resorts International (MGM.N) is discussing making a bid to purchase Barry Diller’s People Inc (PPLI.O) , the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, a day after People Inc [USN:L4N45F1IF TEXT:"withdrew"] its proposal to buy MGM Resorts. If it decides to proceed, MGM could make its proposal in the coming days, the report added, citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

item.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong joins 40/40 club as Cubs clinch wild-card spot
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong became the seventh player in MLB history with a 40-40 season, as he stole his 40th base of the season Thursday, the same day his Chicago Cubs clinched a playoff berth.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pete Crow-Armstrong became the seventh player in MLB history with a 40-40 season, as he stole his 40th base of the season Thursday, the same day his Chicago Cubs clinched a playoff berth. Crow-Armstrong, who is tied for the MLB lead with 45 home runs, joins Jose Canseco (1988), Barry Bonds (1996), Alex Rodriguez (1998), Alfonso Soriano (2006), Ronald Acuna Jr. (2023) and Shohei Ohtani (2024) as the only players to collect at least 40 homers and 40 steals in a season. The favorite for National League Most Valuable Player walked to lead off the first inning against the visiting Miami Marlins and promptly stole second base. He was stranded at third that inning, but the Cubs (88-71) went on to beat the Marlins 2-1 to lock in their NL wild-card playoff spot with three games to go. Crow-Armstrong, 24, has played in all 159 games for the Cubs this season and batted .280 with 107 RBIs. His 45 long balls are tied with Philadelphia's Kyle Schwarber for the major league lead. --Field Level Media

item.title: Police arrest actors, politicians protesting against Netanyahu outside UN
item.description: Police arrested at least 30 people including actors and politicians as they protested outside United Nations headquarters on Thursday against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of his speech at the General Assembly.
item.dc:creator: Maria Tsvetkova
item.content:encoded: Police arrested at least 30 people including actors and politicians as they protested outside United Nations headquarters on Thursday against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of his speech at the General Assembly. Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon, Emmy winner Hannah Einbinder, Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and New York City council member Chi Osse were among those arrested. “What’s being done to Gaza, the obliteration of an entire society, in our name, with our tax dollars, this is our responsibility to speak out against, and Netanyahu has no right to use the platform of the United Nations to justify these atrocities,” said Manijeh Moradian, a 50-year-old university professor of Iranian and Jewish heritage, who took part in the protest. At the General Assembly, Netanyahu [USN:L1N45G05J TEXT:"defended Israel's actions"] in the region, seeking to counter growing international isolation ahead of elections he could lose, as dozens of delegates streamed out of the General Assembly Hall. The rally was organized by Jewish Voice for Peace, a Jewish activist group that supports Palestinians. Around 200 people gathered outside the United Nations in identical white T-shirts with printed slogans "Fund people not bombs," "No war" and "Free Palestine." The group blocked traffic, and police ordered them to leave through loudspeakers. Some people moved to the sidewalks, but the core group of protesters remained seated on the pavement and continued chanting anti-Netanyahu slogans as police officers, who arrived on bicycles, surrounded them. One by one officers pulled protesters from the group, tied their hands behind their backs with zip ties and escorted them to police buses. The activists kept chanting "Netanyahu go to hell" outside the buses.

item.title: Índice de pobreza põe Milei à prova na Argentina antes das eleições
item.description: Sopas comunitárias lotadas, o ressurgimento de clubes de troca e famílias que recorrem a empréstimos de curto prazo para comprar mantimentos estão evidenciando tensões sociais crescentes na Argentina, enquanto economistas esperam que dados oficiais divulgados nesta quinta-feira mostrem o primeiro aumento da pobreza desde que o presidente Javier Milei controlou a inflação.
item.dc:creator: Nicolás Misculin
item.content:encoded: Sopas comunitárias lotadas, o ressurgimento de clubes de troca e famílias que recorrem a empréstimos de curto prazo para comprar mantimentos estão evidenciando tensões sociais crescentes na Argentina, enquanto economistas esperam que dados oficiais divulgados nesta quinta-feira mostrem o primeiro aumento da pobreza desde que o presidente Javier Milei controlou a inflação. O Instituto Nacional de Estatística e Censos (Indec) da Argentina informou que a pobreza atingiu 32,3% da população no primeiro semestre de 2026, ante 28,2% registrados no período anterior. As estimativas da Universidade Católica da Argentina (UCA) são consideradas um indicador antecipado das tendências oficiais de pobreza. Elas sugerem que a taxa pode subir para 35% da população até o final do ano, revertendo parte de uma queda acentuada que reduziu a taxa para 28% em 2025 e marcando um revés para Milei pouco mais de um ano antes da próxima eleição presidencial na Argentina. “A cada trimestre, nos últimos quatro trimestres, entre 400 mil e 450 mil pessoas caíram na pobreza”, disse Agustín Salvia, diretor do Observatório Argentino da Dívida Social da UCA, que previu que a taxa de pobreza se situa atualmente entre 31% e 32%. Se confirmado, o aumento ainda deixaria a pobreza bem abaixo dos níveis observados durante o primeiro ano de mandato de Milei. Analistas afirmam que isso poderia indicar que os avanços sociais impulsionados pela desaceleração da inflação estão perdendo força, com novos progressos cada vez mais dependentes de uma criação de empregos mais robusta e do crescimento dos salários reais. “Um aumento modesto da pobreza não anularia a grande redução observada sob o governo de Milei, mas sugeriria que a parte mais fácil da melhora já chegou ao fim”, afirmou Nicholas Watson, diretor-gerente para a América Latina da consultoria Teneo. TENSÕES ECONÔMICAS TESTAM APOIO Milei chegou ao poder no final de 2023 com forte apoio de eleitores de baixa e média renda, indignados com anos de inflação galopante. Embora seu governo libertário tenha desacelerado drasticamente a alta dos preços e estabilizado as finanças públicas, organizações sociais e profissionais de assistência social afirmam que mais argentinos estão tendo dificuldades para pagar as contas. Em um salão comunitário nos arredores de Buenos Aires, Ana Barreto ajuda a administrar um clube de troca, onde moradores trocam mercadorias em vez de usar dinheiro. “A pobreza se agravou drasticamente”, disse Barreto, uma professora que fundou o clube em agosto em Villa Astolfi, revivendo uma prática associada a crises econômicas do passado. Óleo de cozinha, açúcar, farinha e macarrão estão entre os itens mais procurados, disse ela, frequentemente trocados por roupas usadas e utensílios domésticos. As dificuldades crescentes parecem estar prejudicando o apoio entre os eleitores de baixa renda, à medida que Milei avança rumo a uma provável candidatura à reeleição em 2027. As últimas pesquisas de opinião mostram que o índice de aprovação de Milei caiu drasticamente entre os entrevistados mais pobres, levantando dúvidas sobre se ele conseguirá manter uma base eleitoral que foi fundamental para sua vitória na eleição anterior. Uma pesquisa da AtlasIntel realizada em setembro revelou que a desaprovação entre os entrevistados de baixa renda — definidos como aqueles que ganham até cerca de US$650 por mês — subiu para quase 70%, enquanto a aprovação caiu para menos de 30%. Um ano antes, os números eram de 57% e 37%, respectivamente. Em nível nacional, 58% desaprovam Milei, enquanto 38,1% o aprovam. INFLAÇÃO MAIS BAIXA NÃO É MAIS SUFICIENTE Cortes nos salários do setor público, a eliminação de subsídios para transporte e serviços públicos e a flexibilização das regras de importação pressionaram as famílias e oneraram alguns setores com foco no mercado interno. O governo de Milei afirma que as medidas de austeridade são necessárias para restaurar a estabilidade econômica, eliminando os déficits orçamentários crônicos que contribuíram para repetidas crises econômicas e alta inflação. Argumenta que equilibrar o orçamento e gerar um superávit fiscal fortalecerá as finanças públicas, tranquilizará os investidores e criará as condições para um crescimento sustentável. Mas Gustavo Raúl Pérez, dono de uma loja de ferragens em San Fernando, ao norte de Buenos Aires, disse que seu negócio foi prejudicado porque os clientes não têm mais condições de comprar. “Quatro anos atrás, eu tinha filas de clientes. Eu vendia dez carrinhos de mão; agora vendo apenas um”, disse Pérez. “Votei em Milei acreditando que ele traria mudanças para melhor, mas ele realmente me decepcionou”, acrescentou Pérez. O desemprego subiu para 7,9% no segundo trimestre deste ano, ante 7,6% no mesmo período de 2025. O emprego no setor privado vem caindo há 13 meses consecutivos e a recuperação da renda das famílias estagnou em grande parte, disse Watson. O governo afirma que manterá o rumo. “O presidente não vai se desviar nem um milímetro de seu programa. Ele não vai flexibilizar sua política monetária (contracionista) para ganhar eleições”, disse um porta-voz do governo à Reuters. O governo de Milei se recusou a aumentar os gastos públicos ou renovar subsídios — medidas frequentemente utilizadas em anos eleitorais —, argumentando que isso comprometeria seus esforços para conter a inflação e manter a disciplina fiscal. Em outro clube de troca criado há dois anos, Melany Malén Borré disse que muitos se sentem frustrados porque as melhorias em seus padrões de vida não se concretizaram. “Acho que as pessoas que votaram em Milei esperavam um progresso que nunca aconteceu”, disse Borré. (Reportagem de Nicolás Misculin, reportagem adicional de Miguel Lo Bianco)

item.title: Lula deve anunciar veto total às bets e linha de crédito para clubes de futebol, dizem fontes
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva deve apresentar na sexta-feira uma medida provisória para proibir totalmente as apostas online no país e, ao mesmo tempo, oferecer uma linha de crédito com juros mais baixos aos clubes de futebol para minimizar o impacto da perda de patrocínio, disseram fontes do governo que acompanham as discussões sobre tema.
item.dc:creator: Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva deve apresentar na sexta-feira uma medida provisória para proibir totalmente as apostas online no país e, ao mesmo tempo, oferecer uma linha de crédito com juros mais baixos aos clubes de futebol para minimizar o impacto da perda de patrocínio, disseram fontes do governo que acompanham as discussões sobre tema. De acordo com as fontes ouvidas pela Reuters, a decisão ainda não está 100% tomada porque estão sendo analisadas as bases técnicas e jurídicas para a medida, que iria além de uma ideia inicial de banir apenas os chamados cassinos online. O veto total foi um pedido de Lula à equipe, afirmaram as fontes. Na semana passada, como mostrou a Reuters, a tendência do governo era proibir apenas os cassinos -- que representam cerca de 70% da arrecadação dos sites de apostas -- e restringir a propaganda dessas empresas. No entanto, a avaliação do presidente, que é candidato à reeleição, foi de que a proibição total faria mais sentido para a população. Uma pesquisa Atlas/Bloomberg divulgada esta semana apontou que 71% dos entrevistados "concordam totalmente" com a proibição das bets, e apenas 13% "discordam totalmente." Ao mesmo tempo, o levantamento apontou que 36% dos entrevistados avaliam que a disseminação das bets foi causada pelo governo Lula, enquanto 25% consideram que foi pelo governo Jair Bolsonaro. Na verdade, a liberação das apostas esportivas no Brasil aconteceu em 2018, ainda no governo de Michel Temer. FINANCIAMENTO PARA OS CLUBES Em meio às notícias sobre as discussões no governo a respeito das restrições às bets, houve uma forte reação contrária dos clubes de futebol. Na semana passada, os principais clubes do país divulgaram uma nota contra a intenção do governo, alegando que a retirada do recurso de patrocínios -- cerca de R$1 bilhão por ano -- iria "acabar com o futebol". Apesar de uma reação forte nas redes sociais contra os clubes, o governo reconhece que pode haver um impacto inicial pela proibição das bets até que os patrocínios se reacomodem. Por esse motivo, o governo irá criar uma linha de crédito com juros mais baixos, em uma tentativa de diminuir um pouco a resistência. Lula planeja fazer o anúncio das duas medidas na sexta-feira, em São Paulo. Ao mesmo tempo, deve ser anunciada uma nova medida do governo para combater o endividamento da população -- o terceiro programa do governo para tentar reduzir as dívidas. O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, disse na semana passada, em entrevista ao jornal Extra, que a proposta consiste na compra com deságios altos de dívidas não pagas de pessoas físicas que os bancos ou empresas já tenham considerado, ou estejam perto de considerar, como perdas.

item.title: Microsoft President Brad Smith to lead communications department
item.description: Microsoft President Brad Smith will oversee the company's communications department, a company spokesperson confirmed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Microsoft President Brad Smith will oversee the company's communications department, a company spokesperson confirmed on Thursday. The change puts Smith, one of Microsoft's most prominent public-facing executives, in charge of corporate communications as the company faces issues ranging from artificial intelligence to regulation. Smith has become a prominent voice for Microsoft on public policy issues, including AI governance, technology regulation and the geopolitical implications of the company's global expansion. Brent Colburn, vice president for global public affairs, will serve as interim communications leader during the transition, the spokesperson said. Smith joined Microsoft in 1993, and in 2002 he was named Microsoft's general counsel, a role in which he spent the next decade leading the company's efforts to resolve antitrust disputes with governments around the world and companies across the technology sector.

item.title: Rangers improve playoff hopes with win over Mets
item.description: Kumar Rocker pitched five solid innings on Thursday afternoon for the Texas Rangers, who salvaged the finale of a three-game series and boosted their playoff hopes with a 3-1 victory over the New York Mets in Arlington, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kumar Rocker pitched five solid innings on Thursday afternoon for the Texas Rangers, who salvaged the finale of a three-game series and boosted their playoff hopes with a 3-1 victory over the New York Mets in Arlington, Texas. Josh Jung hit the go-ahead, two-run homer in the first and Corey Seager went deep in the fourth for the Rangers (79-80), who opened the day tied with the Houston Astros for first place in the American League West. The Astros were scheduled to open a season-ending, four-game series against the Athletics later Thursday in West Sacramento, Calif. Houston won the season series over the Rangers 9-4, meaning Texas must take the division outright. Jung finished 3-for-3 and raised his season average to .299. Carson Benge had an RBI double in the first inning for the Mets (73-86), who entered Thursday two games behind the Washington Nationals to sit in last place in the National League East. The teams are scheduled to play in the final series of the season this weekend in Washington. New York hasn't finished in last place since 2003. Rocker (6-11) allowed one run on three hits and two walks while striking out four in his first start against the Mets, who drafted but did not sign him in 2021 due to concerns over his arm. Robert Garcia, Tyler Alexander and Chase Silseth combined for three innings of one-hit ball before Jordan Montgomery recorded his first save of the season and the second of his nine-year career with a perfect ninth. Montgomery recorded his first save on Sept, 11, 2024, when he tossed the final three innings for the Arizona Diamondbacks in their 14-4 win over the Rangers. Zac Thornton (5-6) took the hard-luck loss for the Mets after allowing two runs on four hits and one walk while striking out four over five innings. The left-hander finished his rookie season with a 3.42 ERA in 15 starts. Four players had a hit apiece for the Mets -- including Brett Baty, whose single in the seventh inning extended his on-base streak to 17 straight games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Airbus identifies A321neo quality issue, says no safety risk
item.description: Airbus said on Thursday it had identified a quality defect that could reduce corrosion resistance inside the fuselage structure of A321neos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Airbus (AIR.PA) said on Thursday it had identified a quality defect that could reduce corrosion resistance inside the fuselage structure of A321neos. Air Current earlier reported that the issue could affect more than 500 aircraft. The plane maker said aircraft can continue to operate as it was a quality issue, not a safety issue. The source of the issue has been identified, contained and a remedy is available, the company added.

item.title: Soja recua em Chicago enquanto mercado acompanha encontro entre Trump e Xi
item.description: Os contratos futuros de soja na bolsa de Chicago (CBOT) registraram queda nesta quinta-feira, enquanto os operadores aguardavam para ver se a visita do presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, à Casa Branca impulsionaria a demanda da China por produtos dos EUA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de soja na bolsa de Chicago (CBOT) registraram queda nesta quinta-feira, enquanto os operadores aguardavam para ver se a visita do presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, à Casa Branca impulsionaria a demanda da China por produtos dos EUA. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, recebeu Xi na Casa Branca para uma cúpula de Estado pomposa, que se espera que seja rica em simbolismo, mas pobre em conteúdo. Alguns operadores do mercado de grãos estavam ficando impacientes com a falta de notícias concretas sobre acordos comerciais resultantes da cúpula. O secretário do Treasury dos EUA, Scott Bessent, disse à Fox News na quarta-feira, após conversas com o vice-primeiro-ministro chinês He Lifeng, que eles haviam concordado em prorrogar até 10 de janeiro um acordo que suspendeu uma guerra comercial em que as tarifas mútuas chegaram a ultrapassar 100%. Exportadores privados relataram vendas de 120.000 toneladas métricas de soja dos EUA para a China, informou o Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA (USDA) em seu sistema de relatórios diários. O contrato de soja novembro da CBOT fechou em queda de 0,50 centavo, a US$13,17-1/2 por bushel. O milho fechou em baixa de 1,50 centavo, a US$5,2750 por bushel, também sob influência das expectativas em torno do encontro de Xi com Trump. Os contratos futuros de trigo caíram para a mínima em quatro semanas nesta quinta-feira, devido às crescentes esperanças de uma recuperação nas exportações de grãos da região do Mar Negro, segundo analistas. Os renovados esforços diplomáticos para pôr fim à guerra na Ucrânia mantiveram a atenção dos operadores voltada para as perspectivas dos embarques do Mar Negro. O contrato de trigo dezembro na CBOT fechou em queda de 1,50 centavo, a US$7,07 por bushel. (Reportagem de Tom Polansek)

item.title: Yankees place RHP Clarke Schmidt (biceps) on IL
item.description: The New York Yankees placed right-hander Clarke Schmidt on the 15-day injured list with right biceps neuritis Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Yankees placed right-hander Clarke Schmidt on the 15-day injured list with right biceps neuritis Thursday. The move is retroactive to Monday. The club recalled right-hander Bradley Hanner from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre in a corresponding move. Schmidt had his second Tommy John surgery in the summer of 2025 and was not activated until earlier this month. In his one and only appearance, he gave up two hits and struck out two in two-thirds of an inning Sept. 16 during a 5-4, 13-inning loss to the Minnesota Twins. Now, he will be shelved until at least Oct. 6, ruling him out for the American League wild-card round. Schmidt, 30, was a starter for the Yankees from 2023-25 but worked in relief before that. In 98 career games (67 starts), he is 23-24 with two saves, a 3.81 ERA, 139 walks and 386 strikeouts across 394 innings. Hanner, 27, made his major league debut on Aug. 14 and played four games, pitching to an 11.81 ERA (seven earned runs in 5 1/3 innings) without a decision. --Field Level Media

item.title: Açúcar bruto recua na bolsa ICE, café arábica volta a se aproximar da mínima de 3 meses
item.description: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE se estabilizaram nesta quinta-feira, após atingirem uma máxima de uma semana no início do dia, enquanto o café arábica voltou a se aproximar de uma mínima de três meses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE se estabilizaram nesta quinta-feira, após atingirem uma máxima de uma semana no início do dia, enquanto o café arábica voltou a se aproximar de uma mínima de três meses. AÇÚCAR * O contrato de açúcar bruto fechou em queda de 0,17 centavo, ou 1%, a 17,58 centavos por libra-peso, após ter atingido 18,02 centavos/libra-peso no início do pregão. * A produção de açúcar na região centro-sul do Brasil, principal área produtora, deve ter caído 42,5% na primeira quinzena de setembro, depois que as chuvas atrapalharam a colheita, de acordo com uma pesquisa com dez analistas publicada pela equipe da S&P Global na noite de quarta-feira. * "Estamos vendo mais atrasos na moagem relacionados às chuvas (no Brasil) e há previsão de mais chuvas na primeira semana de outubro. O mercado ainda pode testar os 18,60", disse o corretor e consultor independente Michael McDougall. * Ele também observou que o aumento dos preços do petróleo está impulsionando a alta do açúcar, mas acrescentou que a demanda continua fraca. * A Índia, por exemplo, está se aproximando de novas regulamentações para restringir a venda de alimentos gordurosos e açucarados em um raio de 50 metros das escolas, a mais recente proposta para reduzir o consumo de "junk food" no país. * O preço do açúcar branco subiu 0,8%, para US$509,90 por tonelada métrica. CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou em queda de 0,55 centavo, ou 0,2%, a US$2,7535 por libra-peso, voltando-se para a mínima de três meses registrada na terça-feira, de US$2,6300. * A safra de café de 2026 do Brasil, maior produtor mundial, deve totalizar um recorde de 67,6 milhões de sacas de 60 kg, informou a agência nacional Conab, elevando sua estimativa anterior de 66,7 milhões, já que as produtividades mais altas do arábica mais do que compensaram a menor produção de robusta. * "Persiste a incerteza sobre o que um super El Niño poderia significar para o enchimento dos grãos no Brasil e sobre as condições de seca que ele normalmente traz para a Indonésia", afirmou a Cardiff Coffee Trading em uma nota, acrescentando que as condições permanecem satisfatórias por enquanto. * O contrato de futuro do café robusta caiu 0,8%, para US$3.290 por tonelada, após atingir na terça-feira a menor cotação em três meses e meio, de US$3.218. * "A oferta robusta do Brasil e o aumento constante das exportações do Vietnã estão pressionando os preços do robusta", disse um trader baseado no Vietnã, principal produtor de robusta. CACAU * O cacau em Londres fechou com alta de £55, ou 1,3%, a £4.183 por tonelada. * Gana, segundo maior produtor de cacau, dará início à sua safra de 2026/27 na sexta-feira e anunciará o preço na origem para a safra, segundo informaram cinco fontes à Reuters. * A corretora ADMIS informou que as chuvas devem continuar nos próximos dez dias na África Ocidental, principal região produtora, aliviando as preocupações com a safra 2026/27. * O contrato futuro de cacau de Nova York subiu 1,1%, para US$5.590 por tonelada. (Reportagem de May Angel e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: 'Name is... Juice': Juszczyk appeals fine over alleged beer-drinking celebration
item.description: San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk has filed an appeal against a fine he received from the NFL this week, after the league said he had imitated swigging a beer during an on-field celebration.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk has filed an appeal against a fine he received from the NFL this week, after the league said he had imitated swigging a beer during an on-field celebration. The incident happened during the Niners' 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins, during which Juszczyk tipped his head back and mimed taking a celebratory sip, which the 10-times Pro Bowler later said was a nod to his nickname "Juice". The NFL saw it differently, confirming reports that the gesture was seen as mimicking drinking beer, which breaks rules forbidding engaging in offensive demonstrations. The league also confirmed reports that Juszczyk had appealed the fine. ESPN's NFL insider Adam Schefter reported that the Harvard grad texted him: "I don’t even drink beer!" The 35-year-old also made his case on social media, posting several examples of him doing the same celebration, including one with the caption "Fresh squeezed juice". "Name is…Juice," he wrote in another post on Instagram.

View this post on Instagram

item.title: Petróleo fecha em alta de cerca de 3% após ataque dos houthis à Arábia Saudita
item.description: Os preços do petróleo subiram cerca de 3% nesta quinta-feira, atingindo a maior cotação em uma semana, depois que um ataque com mísseis dos houthis contra a Arábia Saudita reacendeu os temores de interrupções no abastecimento.
item.dc:creator: Scott Disavino
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo subiram cerca de 3% nesta quinta-feira, atingindo a maior cotação em uma semana, depois que um ataque com mísseis dos houthis contra a Arábia Saudita reacendeu os temores de interrupções no abastecimento. No entanto, as negociações foram voláteis e os preços recuaram em relação às máximas do pregão após notícias de que os EUA e o Irã discutiram a reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz. Os futuros do Brent subiram US$3,52, ou 3,4%, fechando a US$106,60 o barril. O petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos EUA subiu US$2,45, ou 2,7%, fechando a US$ 94,61. Em suas máximas da sessão, ambos os contratos registraram alta de cerca de 5%. O Brent registrou seu maior fechamento desde 15 de setembro. Foi a primeira alta em dias para o WTI, que havia caído 13% nas seis sessões anteriores. A Arábia Saudita interceptou seis mísseis balísticos disparados pelos houthis do Iêmen, apoiados pelo Irã, frustrando ataques à província de Taif, no sul do país, e à região de Yanbu, no Mar Vermelho, informou a coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita no Iêmen. Companhias aéreas iranianas foram proibidas de operar em países vizinhos, incluindo os Emirados Árabes Unidos e Omã, em resposta às novas sanções dos EUA -- o primeiro grande impacto de uma mudança na política norte-americana para atingir empresas de países terceiros que fazem negócios com o Irã. Com a guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã praticamente estagnada há meses no campo de batalha, Washington anunciou uma extensão de suas sanções financeiras, visando empresas de países terceiros que fazem negócios com empresas iranianas -- uma prática conhecida como “sanções secundárias”. Na quarta-feira, o Irã ameaçou retaliar contra os países vizinhos que cumprirem a proibição dos EUA aos seus voos, tornando seus aeroportos “inutilizáveis”. Por outro lado, a Arábia Saudita está aumentando os volumes de bombeamento de petróleo por meio de seu oleoduto Leste-Oeste, que se estende até Yanbu, seu centro de exportação no Mar Vermelho, embora os carregamentos de petroleiros ainda não tenham sido retomados, de acordo com fontes do setor, imagens de satélite e dados de transporte marítimo.

item.title: Late Gakpo equaliser earns Dutch 1-1 draw against Germany to spoil Klopp's debut
item.description: Cody Gakpo volleyed in a stoppage-time equaliser to rescue a 1-1 draw for the Netherlands against Germany in their Nations League Group A2 opener on Thursday, denying new coach Juergen Klopp a winning start.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cody Gakpo volleyed in a stoppage-time equaliser to rescue a 1-1 draw for the Netherlands against Germany in their Nations League Group A2 opener on Thursday, denying new coach Juergen Klopp a winning start. Former Liverpool manager Klopp, who [USN:L1N43Q095 TEXT:"took charge of"] Germany in July following their shock early World Cup exit following defeat by Paraguay, looked to have made a winning start before Gakpo rounded off a quick counter-attack. That gave new Netherlands coach, Xavi Hernandez, appointed in August after Ronald Koeman stepped down following their World Cup round of 32 elimination, something to smile about. Xavi is the first foreigner in charge of the Dutch national team since the 1978 World Cup. "We have to accept the result," Klopp said. "Even though I badly wanted to win I take the draw." "I was very, very, very pleased with a lot of the individual performances. Overall, I was very happy with the passion we showed. We can play better and play more football, that’s for sure," he said. The Germans got bad news before the start with playmaker Jamal Musiala ruled out after feeling muscle pain during the warm-up, but they still made a high-tempo start. They were left stunned in the 13th minute when Dutch captain Virgil van Dijk headed in from a corner but his effort was overruled by VAR for a foul on Germany keeper Marc-Andre ter Stegen. There was more bad news for Klopp's team with forward Kai Havertz taken off injured in the 30th, but the visitors took the lead two minutes later with Felix Nmecha slotting in from close range. Karim Adeyemi should have scored again but he somehow missed the target from five metres out. The Dutch upped the pressure after the break and repeatedly came close to an equaliser with Germany's new number one Ter Stegen making several good saves. But their dominance finally paid off with Gakpo's late strike. "We deserved at least a point," van Dijk said. "We played well at times.. but after only three days working it was a good performance." HAALAND WINNER In their Scandinavian Group A4 clash, Norway's Erling Haaland struck twice, including a 74th-minute winner, to edge his team past Denmark 3-2 in Oslo and earn their first competitive win over their opponents. "It tasted sweet. It feels great to beat our neighbours," captain Martin Odegaard said. "There is a lot we could have done better, but even when we were put under pressure, we found a way back and responded." The Danes had powered back from a two-goal deficit and levelled on the hour after first-half goals from Oscar Bobb and Haaland had put the hosts 2-0 up. Norway were left with 10 men in stoppage time after David Moller Wolfe was sent off following a second booking. Veteran Cristiano Ronaldo had a goal disallowed but Portugal still earned a 1-0 victory over Wales courtesy of Joao Felix's 22nd minute long-range winner in a successful start for the defending Nations League champions' new coach Jorge Jesus. Wales had several golden chances in the second half and hit the crossbar through Brennan Johnson before Portugal defender Ruben Dias made two key blocks to protect their lead. Saied Abu Farchi scored in the 55th minute for Israel in their League B 3-1 defeat by hosts Austria, but the player was [USN:L6N45G19K TEXT:"sent off"] after a second booking following his celebration where he simulated a gun with the corner flag. Romano Schmid had given Austria a 43rd-minute lead with a penalty and the hosts struck twice more late in the game to earn the three points. There was drama in Belgrade where visitors Greece came from a goal down to snatch a 2-1 victory over Serbia thanks to Tasos Douvikas' winner deep in stoppage time. French-born players scored every goal as Malta came from behind to beat Andorra 2-1 in their Nations League D clash. Irvin Cardona and Teddy Teuma took turns as scorer and provider to secure Malta’s victory after fellow French-born forward Guillaume Lopez had put the hosts ahead.

item.title: パレスチナ議長、20年ぶり評議会選実施を再表明 国連総会でビデオ演説
item.description:
Nidal al-Mughrabi Ali Sawafta
[２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Nidal al-Mughrabi　Ali Sawafta

[２４日　ロイター] - パレスチナ自治政府のアッバス議長は２４日、ニューヨークで開かれている国連総会の一般討論でビデオ演説し、立法評議会（議会）選挙を１１月２８日に実施する計画を改めて表明した。実現すれば約２０年ぶりの選挙となる。国内では実施を疑問視する見方が根強いものの、国際社会が支持する改革を前進させる狙いがある。

アッバス氏は、「われわれは国民と国際社会に対して約束した国家改革計画を完了させた」と説明。その上で「１１月２８日の立法評議会選挙に向けて前進している」と述べた。

アッバス氏は、汚職や統治の問題に対処するための改革を実施するよう米国から圧力を受けており、米国側は同氏がこうした改革を実行してこなかったと非難している。

パレスチナでは、２００５─０６年の選挙以降、評議会選挙も議長選も実施されていない。その後、イスラム組織ハマスがパレスチナ自治区ガザを掌握し、アッバス氏の側近らを追放した。アッバス氏は今年、２０２７年に議長選挙を実施するとの議長令を出したが、具体的な日程はまだ決まっていない。

一方、アッバス氏が率いる自治政府主流派ファタハ幹部らは、選挙の実施を疑問視している。同氏は立法評議会選挙の実施を約束している一方で、ファタハ内部からの要請を含め、議長選の実施を求める声には応じていない。

アッバス氏はまた、パレスチナ代表団の国連本部への立ち入りを制限した米国の措置を批判し、開催国としての義務違反だと非難。米国が自身へのビザ発給を再び拒否したことにも言及し、「われわれはこうした違法な懲罰的措置と、その根拠となる非難や正当化を拒絶する」と述べた。

item.title: Finnish leader pleads with Musk to help Ukraine hit Russian missile launchers
item.description: Finnish President Alexander Stubb said on Thursday he pleaded with SpaceX owner Elon Musk to expand Starlink satellite internet coverage for Ukraine so it can strike Russian ballistic missile launchers located inside Russian territory.
item.dc:creator: Tom Balmforth
item.content:encoded: Finnish President Alexander Stubb said on Thursday he pleaded with SpaceX owner Elon Musk to expand Starlink satellite internet coverage for Ukraine so it can strike Russian ballistic missile launchers located inside Russian territory. With winter looming, Ukraine has an acute shortage of air defenses to repel Russian ballistic missiles, and Kyiv officials believe that turning on Starlink over Russian territory would help it target the Russian launchers that fire the missiles. "That's why ... I plead that Elon Musk would give the Ukrainians the possibility to use Starlink in areas where there are ballistic missile launchers, either in the occupied territory of Ukraine or in Russia for strategic purposes because that would save lives," Stubb said. The Finnish leader, a staunch ally of Ukraine who also has good relations with US President Donald Trump, made the remark in an interview with Reuters in New York where world leaders have converged for the annual gathering at the United Nations. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy used the event to press hard for [USN:L1N45F0K5 TEXT:"ceasefires"] that would cover strikes on targets related to energy infrastructure and vessels in the Black Sea. Russia has given no public indication it wants to see such arrangements. Four-and-a-half years since the full-scale Russian invasion, the Ukrainians fear Moscow plans to systematically target and destroy power and heating sites in the depth of winter. Russia's use of ballistic missiles hit record levels this summer. Only Ukraine's Patriot air defenses are able to intercept such missiles, but ammunition is severely depleted and it is unclear where new supplies could come from. Musk switched on the Starlink satellite internet service over Ukraine shortly after Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. It has become the lifeblood of Ukraine's battlefield communications and a tool for piloting drones. Starlink does not work over Russian territory, but Ukrainian officials believe turning it on for Ukraine's use inside Russia would allow its weapons to strike mobile ballistic launchers located within several hundred kilometres of the border. Looking ahead to winter, Stubb said there were three things that Ukraine needed. "One is air defenses and even Starlink would be to a certain extent a good air defense there. And the second one is energy installations for the winter." "The third one is money. So those are the things that we're working on. We're working on putting up a winter package because I don't see the war ending, you know, before the winter." Stubb said it was good that US-led peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine had restarted in August with the visits of US envoys to both Moscow and Kyiv. "I still think that the easiest solution would be to call an unconditional ceasefire, basically stop the killing, as President Trump reiterated in his speech in the UN General Assembly," he said. Such a step, he continued, would be followed by negotiations on security, territory, reconstruction and compensation and other topics. The war could be frozen along the line of contact with 30-kilometre buffer zones east and west, he said, adding that the next best option was the idea of the partial ceasefire on energy and grain related targets.

item.title: White Sox rout Royals, clinch first playoff berth since 2021
item.description: Miguel Vargas had two hits and two RBIs, Kyle Teel homered and David Sandlin delivered six strong innings as the visiting Chicago White Sox routed the Kansas City Royals 9-1 on Thursday to clinch an American League playoff berth.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Miguel Vargas had two hits and two RBIs, Kyle Teel homered and David Sandlin delivered six strong innings as the visiting Chicago White Sox routed the Kansas City Royals 9-1 on Thursday to clinch an American League playoff berth. Chicago (82-77) is back in the AL postseason for the first time since 2021 after enduring three straight 100-loss seasons. Fueled by an early barrage against Royals right-hander Randy Dobnak, the White Sox moved to a half-game behind the Central Division-leading Cleveland Guardians, who were set to play in Boston later Thursday. Chicago holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over Cleveland and is 3½ games up on the Texas Rangers for the third and final AL wild-card berth. The White Sox scored three runs in each of the first two innings against Kansas City (68-91). Vargas and Tristan Peters contributed RBI singles in the first inning while Vargas added another run-scoring single in the second. Sandlin, a rookie righty, pitched comfortably with the lead. He worked around Bobby Witt Jr.'s one-out double to escape the first inning in 17 pitches and needed 85 pitches to complete his outing. Sandlin (3-2) yielded one run and five hits with zero walks against seven strikeouts. Dobnak (3-5) allowed six runs (four earned) and six hits in 1 1/3 innings. He had one walk and one strikeout while throwing a wild pitch and committing an error on a pickoff attempt. Teel reached reliever Alex Lange for a solo shot to start the fourth and Peters had an RBI forceout later in the inning. Salvador Perez homered leading off the bottom of the fourth to bring the Royals to within 8-1. It marked Perez's 20th round-tripper this season, his sixth consecutive campaign reaching that plateau. John Rave and Jason Isbel had two hits apiece for Kansas City. Witt Jr. has reached base in 21 consecutive games. Sam Antonacci, Chase Meidroth, Braden Montgomery and Teel joined Vargas with two-hit efforts for Chicago. Andrew Benintendi and Peters also had two RBIs. Chicago won the season series from Kansas City 9-4. The White Sox have won four of five while the Royals have lost six of seven. --Field Level Media

item.title: Inside Reuters' calculation of Australia's housing market ripple effects
item.description: For most Australian homeowners, the cost of the country's sharpest housing downturn in years has been the modest fall in property values since interest rates began rising in February.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: For most Australian homeowners, the cost of the country's sharpest housing downturn in years has been the modest fall in property values since interest rates began rising in February. But while prices have dipped only slightly, home sales have fallen sharply. Reuters set out to [USN:L4N45008Y TEXT:"measure the impact"] on the businesses that depend on housing turnover. Those businesses span a vast ecosystem built during Australia's quarter-century property boom. Real estate agents, conveyancers, auctioneers, property listing sites, furniture stagers and building inspectors largely earn revenue when homes change hands. Removalists, painters, landscapers, renovators and furniture retailers are also exposed to sales activity, though they make money elsewhere too. To estimate the economic impact, Reuters calculated the commercial spending typically generated when an Australian sells a home, buys another and moves. The analysis covered costs from agent commissions and listing preparations through settlement, moving expenses and purchases of furniture and appliances. Low and high estimates of individual goods were used to derive an impact range. State governments were excluded, despite collecting large stamp-duty revenues and seeing their [USN:L4N4570GO TEXT:"revenue hit"] by the slowdown, because they are not commercial entities. Banks were also excluded because most housing-related earnings come from mortgage repayments rather than transaction volumes. The analysis was based on Australia's median home price of A$1.11 million ($790,000) and the most common dwelling type, a three-bedroom detached house. For each good or service, Reuters used a mainstream advertised price range rather than extreme outliers. Agent commissions, for example, were assumed at the common 2% to 3% range. A new couch might cost anywhere from A$20 on Marketplace to A$60,000 from an exclusive boutique. Instead, we used the cheapest widely available option (A$219 from Kogan.com.au) and the priciest mainstream offering (A$8,796 from King Furniture), applying the same methodology across all items. Each item was then weighted by the likelihood of the expense occurring. Costs nearly universal to a transaction, such as agent commissions and conveyancing settled on software platform PEXA, received a 100% weighting. Less common expenses received lower weightings. For example, painting a three-bedroom home before sale typically costs A$4,500 to A$10,000, but a 2023 Houzz survey found only a quarter of sellers do so. Pre-sale painting was therefore weighted at 25%. Based on feedback from economists, Reuters also adjusted for the roughly 60-40 split between owner-occupiers and investors. A survey by removalist website Muval found 39% of Australians bought entertainment appliances when moving home, but only about 60% of property purchases are made by owner-occupiers. Television purchases were therefore weighted at 23%. Economists also pointed to the "wealth effect" whereby people spend less when they believe their home's value is falling. We excluded that from our analysis because the project focused solely on spending directly linked to property transactions. Some effects, after all, are much harder to measure. ($1 = 1.4088 Australian dollars)

item.title: Billions in collateral damage: The hidden cost of Australia's housing slowdown
item.description: This time last year, Sydney property stylist Joanne Cauchi was turning away work, buying new furniture and overseeing home installations almost every day.
item.dc:creator: Byron Kaye, Stella Qiu
item.content:encoded: This time last year, Sydney property stylist Joanne Cauchi was turning away work, buying new furniture and overseeing home installations almost every day. Now, her team of three stylists and two removalists handles as few as three jobs a week and has stopped buying inventory altogether. "Usually springtime, and this time of year in particular, is ridiculously busy," said Cauchi. "It is very quiet." The abrupt slowdown illustrates how Australia's housing slump is rippling far beyond real estate agents and mortgage lenders. As higher interest rates and the government's rollback of key property tax concessions sap demand, a sharp drop in home sales is hitting a vast ecosystem of businesses that rely on properties changing hands, from furniture stylists and landscapers to conveyancers, removalists and painters. The damage stems less from falling prices than from a sharp drop in turnover. Home prices are down less than 4% from their March peak and remain above year-ago levels, but far fewer homes are changing hands. A 15% drop in housing turnover since June from a year earlier is stripping an estimated A$355 million to A$710 million ($253 million to $505 million) a month from the property-adjacent economy, according to [USN:L4N45E08X TEXT:"a Reuters analysis"] of the spending triggered when Australians buy, sell and move into a home. Even allowing for annual market swings, housing turnover remains 10.5% below its five-year average, data from property consultant Cotality showed. Reuters calculations suggest that translates into A$2.8 billion to A$5.6 billion less annual spending flowing through businesses that depend on homes changing hands, from furniture retailers and tradespeople to small conveyancing firms. The figure pales beside Australia's A$600 billion-plus annual home sales, but for numerous businesses that depend on housing turnover, it is substantial. The analysis estimated the cost of the goods and services typically purchased when an average three-bedroom detached home changes hands, based on market price ranges and weighted spending patterns from industry or government data. "You get this big dollar number of 'this is how much loss to the economy there is as a result of those lost home purchases'," said James Graham, a University of Sydney senior lecturer who studies housing economics. Graham said the Reuters methodology was reasonable but noted it excluded the "wealth effect", where falling home values weigh on spending by denting confidence. A typical Australian home move triggers spending across a wide range of services, from agents to conveyancers to painters and utility providers, with buyers often also purchasing new furniture and appliances after relocating. "All of the real estate sectors are going to have less income coming in," Graham said. QUICK HIT Property's outsized role in Australia's economy was entrenched by tax incentives introduced over the past quarter century, helping drive Sydney and Melbourne into the ranks of the world's least affordable housing markets. After three interest rate increases since February, the centre-left government took further heat out of the housing market by trimming capital gains tax breaks for existing-home sellers and tightening negative-gearing rules for landlords. A spokesperson for Treasurer Jim Chalmers did not respond to a request for comment. Home sales volumes, which had risen in March, were down 11% in May and 20% in July, according to Cotality. "It's the most severe drop we've seen since the very start of COVID," said Russell Cohen, CEO of conveyancing technology platform PEXA (PXA.AX) , which gets paid when an Australian property sale settles. After growing Australian sales 8% in the year to June, volumes dived 15% in July and stayed there through August, Cohen said in an interview. The slowdown is also hurting corporate earnings. Homewares chain Harvey Norman (HVN.AX) said franchise profit in its June half fell 15%, reversing growth of 14% in the previous six months, citing "reduced appetite for home-related purchases and renovation activity". EXODUS For many businesses, the downturn is already forcing painful choices. At The Moving Box Company, which supplies new and used freight cartons, four factory-floor workers have left since April after having their hours reduced. Headcount has fallen to 9 from 13, leaving managers to take on packing and delivery work themselves. "That's practically how we've had to manage the situation: by reducing the hours of staff," said general manager James Wotherspoon, noting sales were down 19% since June year-on-year. "If we can't give them the hours, I totally respect the fact that they've got to find work elsewhere to survive." For conveyancers and selling agents, the downturn has coincided with the introduction of anti-money laundering rules in July that require greater customer due diligence, adding compliance costs just as revenue is falling. "We're definitely seeing more conversations being had from smaller operators about merging or selling, some retiring out of the industry entirely," said David Winning, founder of Your Move Conveyancing and director of the Australian Institute of Conveyancers NSW Division. The Real Estate Institute of Victoria said 350 of 6,600 agent members planned to cancel their membership, with more than half leaving the profession altogether. "We could expect to see a very significant exodus of sales agents," said Jacob Caine, president of the Real Estate Institute of Australia, by phone. Buyers' agent Zoran Solano said he was ending his office lease and would work remotely after revenue halved since May. "Everyone is being affected," he said. "It's much more widespread than I think people realise." ($1 = 1.4057 Australian dollars)

item.title: Roblox loses bid to halt L.A. County's lawsuit alleging child sex exploitation on gaming platform
item.description: Los Angeles County’s lawsuit accusing Roblox of failing to protect young users from online predators and sexual exploitation will move forward after a judge found that neither federal law nor the US Constitution’s free speech protections shield the gaming platform from the claims.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: Los Angeles County’s lawsuit accusing Roblox (RBLX.N) of failing to protect young users from online predators and sexual exploitation will move forward after a judge found that neither federal law nor the US Constitution’s free speech protections shield the gaming platform from the claims. Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Dean Kitchens on Wednesday rejected Roblox’s bid to dismiss the lawsuit, which alleges Roblox does little to check its users’ ages, allowing kids and adults to interact on its platform with little oversight. Claims about Roblox’s limited age verification are not barred by Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, a federal law protecting online services from liability for user content, because they don’t involve posts on the site by third parties, the judge wrote. Roblox’s choices about how to verify its users’ ages are not expressive features of the platform that would be protected by the US Constitution’s First Amendment, he added. Representatives for Roblox and the county did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Earlier this year, [USN:L4N40T18S TEXT:"Roblox said"] it was making nationwide changes to how teens and children can use its site. In part, the company said it was making changes to its age verification procedures, implementing facial age checks for chat access and introducing age-based accounts with more restrictions and expanding parental controls. A PUBLIC NUISANCE Los Angeles County filed the lawsuit in February. It claims Roblox contributed to an increase in child sex trafficking and exploitation. The county accuses the platform of misleading consumers about its safety and creating a public nuisance by exposing children to sexual exploitation. Public nuisance claims traditionally have targeted conduct that endangers public health or safety, but state governments have increasingly invoked them in litigation involving tobacco, opioids, climate change and vaping. Public nuisance cases allow governments like Los Angeles County to seek court orders forcing companies to make changes to make their products safer, as well as large financial awards to abate the alleged harm. Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin, a Republican, filed a similar public nuisance lawsuit against Roblox in June. That case, which also names chat platform Discord as a defendant, is filed in Los Angeles Superior Court and is ongoing, court records show. Earlier this year, Roblox [USN:L6N41416J TEXT:"struck settlements"] with the attorneys general of Alabama, West Virginia and Nevada, who were investigating the platform for failing to protect young users, but had not yet filed lawsuits. The company agreed to pay more than $30 million and make changes to children's access to its gaming and chat functions. DOZENS OF OTHER CASES Roblox and Discord are facing more than 180 lawsuits filed by people who say they were sexually abused or exploited as minors or filed by their parents, alleging the company failed to warn of the risk and did not take action to protect its young users. The lawsuits allege that conversations between adults and minors that began on Roblox often migrated to Discord. Both companies say they shouldn't be liable for the actions of third parties. As the Los Angeles County litigation moves closer to trial, Roblox and Discord have made efforts to move the individual cases into arbitration. In court filings this week, the companies argued that users agreed to resolve disputes outside of court when they agreed to the sites’ terms and conditions. Lawyers for the people suing say their clients deserve their day in court and will oppose the efforts to send the cases to arbitration. The Los Angeles case is The People of the State of California, acting by and through Los Angeles County Counsel Dawyn Harrison v. Roblox Corp, case number 26STCV05708 in Los Angeles Superior Court. For LA County: Alexandra Walsh of Anapol Weiss For Roblox: Andy Pincus of Mayer Brown

item.title: Trading Day: Rout of control
item.description: The global bond rout continued on Thursday, pushing many key yields around the world to new multi-decade highs. Stock markets around the world felt the heat, although the S&P 500 and Nasdaq staged late rallies to end flat, while oil and the dollar marched higher.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded:
The global bond rout continued on Thursday, pushing many key yields around the world to new multi-decade highs. Stock markets around the world felt the heat, although the [USN:L6N45G0LR TEXT:"S&P 500 and Nasdaq"] staged late rallies to end flat, while [USN:L6N45G01N TEXT:"oil"] and the [USN:L4N45G03F TEXT:"dollar"] marched higher. In [USN:L6N45F0XH TEXT:"my column today"], I look at the dollar's resurgence and soaring bond yields in the context of the US Treasury's recent forays into the FX and bond markets. Right now, "the house" — as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent referred to himself recently — is not winning. Today's Key Reads [USN:FWN45G0T8 TEXT:"Trump says he'll discuss AI with Xi but wants to 'leave it exactly where it is'"] [USN:S0N43U01A TEXT:"US, China agree to extend trade truce by two months, work on bigger deal, Bessent says"] [USN:L8N45G0KO TEXT:"Global bond selloff deepens, as US 30-year yields hit highest since 2004"] [USN:L1N45F0NE TEXT:"US weekly jobless claims near 57-year lows; price reductions boost new home sales"] [USN:L8N45G133 TEXT:"ECB's Schnabel quits to join IMF, setting in motion a board reshuffle"] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: MSCI Asia ex-Japan -0.9%, [USN:L6N45G0EZ TEXT:"Europe"] -0.6%, Wall Street mixed: S&P 500 and Nasdaq flat, Dow -0.3% and a 3-month low. SECTORS/SHARES: Seven sectors on the S&P 500 fall, four rise. Utilities, materials -1%. Comms services +2%. Walmart, IBM -2.5%. Disney +2%. [USN:L4N45G11W TEXT:"Oracle and Blue Owl"] both down ~3.5%. FX: [USN:L4N45G03F TEXT:"Dollar"] hits two-month high, dollar/yen flirts with 159.00. Colombian peso -2%. [USN:L1N45G096 TEXT:"Norwegian, Swedish"] crowns steady after rate decisions. BONDS: French, German yields highest since 2007-08, US 30y yield highest since 2004. US 7y auction weak. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L6N45G01N TEXT:"Oil"] up ~3%, [USN:L4N45G01B TEXT:"gold"] slips ~1%.

Today's Talking Points: No, Mr Bond, I expect you to die The global bond selloff got ugly this week. The rise in yields on Wednesday — ostensibly for "good" reasons of strong business activity data — was exceptional, and pointed to a more worrying breakdown in sentiment. There was little relief on Thursday. Yields are at multi-decade highs in the US, Europe and Japan, but this isn't drawing in buyers en masse. Bond market volatility is now surging too, another reason many investors might sit it out a bit longer. Demand at yesterday's 5-year US bond auction was the lowest in nine years, and the premium demanded by buyers who did show up was one of the highest ever. Today's 7-year auction was also extremely weak. As BofA analysts put it, "the price action likely highlights that investors are not yet comfortable owning bonds in the environment of a Fed restarting the hiking cycle, continued conflict in the Middle East, and a resilient US economy and consumer." An unbridgeable US-China gap Huge fanfare, pomp, and ceremony, but not much substance when it comes to the big issues of the day. Is that a harsh but fair assessment of how the Trump-Xi summit will pan out? True, the US-China trade truce could be extended for another two months to January, and the two sides will agree to further dialogue on AI. But from a market and investment perspective, that's about it. One ironic market curiosity: it is perhaps fitting that on the day Trump and Xi tried to bridge divides and close gaps between the two superpowers, the spread between the two countries' bond yields widened to a record 350 basis points. US borrowing costs are soaring in the face of high inflation, while China’s are sliding as the threat of deflation continues to stalk the economy. Neither side is "winning" on that front. Data center blues Oracle on Thursday declared [USN:L4N45G11W TEXT:""force majeure""] on a massive AI data center project, seeking to protect itself from soaring costs from potential delays in securing power for the "Project Jupiter" venture in New Mexico. Oracle's credit rating sits one notch above junk, and its total debt stands at around $140 billion. Shares fell to a seven-week low on Thursday. But this goes well beyond Oracle. The industry-wide AI capex spend runs into the trillions of dollars, and is increasingly being financed by debt, leasing and other off-balance sheet structures. Many investors were already nervous about the vast cost of building the data centers needed to power the artificial intelligence revolution. This potentially pours fuel on these flames. What could move markets tomorrow? Chinese President Xi Jinping visits US President Donald Trump in Washington Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey speaks US University of Michigan inflation expectations, consumer sentiment (September, final) US durable goods (August) US Federal Reserve officials scheduled to speak include New York Fed President John Williams, Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack Want to receive Trading Day in your inbox every weekday morning? Sign up for my newsletter here . Opinions expressed are those of the author. They do not reflect the views of Reuters News, which, under the Trust Principles , is committed to integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.

item.title: Cubs lock up playoff berth with win over Marlins
item.description: Nico Hoerner ripped a go-ahead RBI single in the sixth and Matthew Boyd tossed seven strong innings, helping the host Chicago Cubs clinch a playoff berth with a 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins on Thursday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nico Hoerner ripped a go-ahead RBI single in the sixth and Matthew Boyd tossed seven strong innings, helping the host Chicago Cubs clinch a playoff berth with a 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins on Thursday afternoon. Chicago's Pete Crow-Armstrong walked to lead off the first inning and promptly stole second base to become the seventh player in MLB history to record at least 40 homers and 40 stolen bases in a single season. Armstrong, who has 45 homers, joined Jose Canseco (1988), Barry Bonds (1996), Alex Rodriguez (1998), Alfonso Soriano (2006), Ronald Acuna Jr. (2023) and Shohei Ohtani (2024) as the only players to reach the 40-40 milestone. Seiya Suzuki belted a solo homer in the fifth inning to highlight his two-hit performance for the Cubs (88-71), who salvaged the finale of their three-game series with Miami. Boyd (10-5) allowed one run on five hits to record his second straight victory following a 0-4 stretch over his previous six starts. Daniel Palencia bridged the gap to Ryan Zeferjahn, who retired the side in order in the ninth inning to secure his seventh save of the season. Jakob Marsee had an RBI single in the third inning for the Marlins (78-81), who have lost four of their last six games. With the game tied 1-1, Ian Happ tripled off Jack Ralston (0-2) to lead off the sixth inning and came home on Hoerner's RBI single to left field. Ralston permitted two runs on three hits in 1 1/3 innings. Brian Navarreto doubled to lead off the third inning against Matthew Boyd before coming home on Marsee's RBI single to center to open the scoring. Suzuki forged a tie in the fifth inning, depositing a 1-0 pitch from Ralston over the wall in center field. The homer was Suzuki's 26th of the season and second in his last four games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Presidente Peña anuncia inversión de 200 millones de dólares para proyecto forestal en Paraguay
item.description: El presidente paraguayo, Santiago Peña, anunció el jueves en Nueva York una inversión de 200 millones de dólares de J.P. Morgan Natural Capital y el grupo local Robinson para un proyecto forestal que se lanzará en el primer trimestre de 2027 en el país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente paraguayo, Santiago Peña, anunció el jueves en Nueva York una inversión de 200 millones de dólares de J.P. Morgan Natural Capital y el grupo local Robinson para un proyecto forestal que se lanzará en el primer trimestre de 2027 en el país. La inversión considera el establecimiento de bosques comerciales, la restauración de bosques nativos y la producción sostenible de madera de alta calidad, según un comunicado de la presidencia paraguaya. La iniciativa prevé el desarrollo en una primera etapa de cerca de 20.000 hectáreas destinadas a la producción de madera. También apunta a la generación de créditos de carbono. "Esta inversión en Paraguay representa una oportunidad atractiva para construir una plataforma forestal escalable y de largo plazo, basada en la gestión sostenible de los recursos y el desarrollo rural", señaló Angela Davis, CEO de J.P. Morgan Natural Capital, según el comunicado.

item.title: Peso mexicano cae a mínimos desde abril tras decisión de Banxico
item.description: El peso mexicano se debilitó el jueves a niveles no vistos en más de cinco meses, luego de que Banco de México mantuvo sin cambios su tasa clave de interés y señaló que sus próximas decisiones dependerán de la evolución de la inflación local.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano se debilitó el jueves a niveles no vistos en más de cinco meses, luego de que [USN:L6N45G177 TEXT:"Banco de México"] mantuvo sin cambios su tasa clave de interés y señaló que sus próximas decisiones dependerán de la evolución de la inflación local.
