item.title: Zelenskiy, Wall Street executives hold talks on Ukraine's reconstruction
item.description: Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy has met with senior Wall Street executives as Kyiv seeks to attract investments to help finance the country's rebuilding efforts.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy has met with senior Wall Street executives as Kyiv seeks to attract investments to help finance the country's rebuilding efforts. The meeting, which took place on Wednesday on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York City, focused mainly around areas such as helping Ukraine get through the winter and supporting its economy, the Ukrainian government said. Ukraine [USN:L8N454050 TEXT:"faces a brutal winter"] as stepped-up Russian strikes on its infrastructure and key export industries deepen the country's budget crisis. The daily cost of the war grew to about $190 million this year. The meeting, attended by more than two dozen US companies, was facilitated by US banking giant Citigroup and the US Chamber of Commerce. Participants also discussed setting up a sovereign wealth fund and strengthening Ukraine's economy with support from members of the International Advisory Group, the Ukrainian government said. "The private sector will play an essential role in the country's reconstruction," Citi CEO Jane Fraser said in a statement. Citi, which has been in Ukraine for more than 25 years, said it was looking to help mobilize investment and support Ukrainian companies. Other attendees included executives from BlackRock (BLK.N) , Franklin Templeton (BEN.N) , Lazard (LAZ.N) , Macquarie (MQG.AX) , State Street (STT.N) , Jane Street, Fairfax (FFH.TO) and McKinsey & Company. Representatives of the US Chamber of Commerce, US International Development Finance Corporation, World Bank, European Investment Bank and European Bank for Reconstruction and Development also participated.

item.title: Vídeo mostra cantor Rick durante pouso de avião, não em queda de helicóptero
item.description: Um vídeo do cantor Rick, da dupla com Renner, dentro de um avião está sendo compartilhado como se mostrasse os momentos que antecederam o recente acidente de helicóptero em que ele morreu, mas as imagens são de de 2023.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo do cantor Rick, da dupla com Renner, dentro de um avião está sendo compartilhado como se mostrasse os momentos que antecederam o recente acidente de helicóptero em que ele morreu, mas as imagens são de de 2023. Estes são os principais detalhes: Posts com o vídeo, que circulam no Facebook, no Instagram e no Threads, mostram o cantor dentro de um avião demonstrando nervosismo com o voo. Legendas nas publicações afirmam se tratar dos momentos antes da queda do helicóptero. “O último vídeo do Rick. Ele já estava sentindo que tinha algo errado. Ele falou que não estava vendo pista nenhuma”, diz uma delas. Uma versão mais longa do vídeo foi publicada no perfil da dupla Rick e Renner no TikTok em agosto de 2023. As imagens mostram que o cantor estava em um avião, e não em um helicóptero, assim como o pouso da aeronave sem intercorrências. Já a queda do helicóptero que transportava Rick aconteceu na segunda-feira passada, 21 de setembro, na serra catarinense, e matou também outras quatro pessoas. Veredicto: Legenda errada. O vídeo mostra Rick em um avião em 2023, e não no helicóptero que caiu nesta semana. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: Spencer Horwitz's sacrifice fly lifts Pirates over Cardinals
item.description: Spencer Horwitz's sacrifice fly in the eighth drove in the go-ahead run, and Paul Skenes concluded his season with a quality start as the Pittsburgh Pirates wrapped up their home schedule with a 2-1 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals on Thursday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Spencer Horwitz's sacrifice fly in the eighth drove in the go-ahead run, and Paul Skenes concluded his season with a quality start as the Pittsburgh Pirates wrapped up their home schedule with a 2-1 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals on Thursday afternoon. Horwitz's fly ball to center was deep enough to allow Ronny Simon to score. Mason Montgomery recorded his 17th save after pitching a scoreless ninth and helping Pittsburgh (81-77) finish .500 or better for the first time since 2018. The Cardinals (77-82) are guaranteed to finish with back-to-back losing seasons for the first time since 1994-95. St. Louis reliever Ryne Stanek (2-3) walked Simon with one out. A wild pitch and a throwing error by catcher Ivan Herrera as Simon was advancing to second allowed him to reach third, setting up Horwitz's RBI. Skenes tossed 6 1/3 innings, struck out eight, walked two and allowed one run on three hits. His final strikeout of Leo Bernal was his 200th for the season and came on his 96th pitch. Skenes became the second Pirates pitcher ever to record 200-plus strikeouts in back-to-back seasons, joining Bob Veale (three straight from 1964-66). Skenes, the National League's Cy Young Award winner last season, struggled at times but finished his 2026 campaign with a 10-11 record and a 3.82 ERA in 32 starts. He allowed one earned run or fewer in 14 of those starts. Alec Burleson belted a solo home run -- his 24th of the season -- off Skenes with two outs in the first inning. Pittsburgh answered in the bottom of the first as Oneil Cruz led off with a double, stole third and scored on an RBI single by Brandon Lowe. Cruz and Konnor Griffin each finished with two hits. The Pirates' bullpen kept the Cardinals scoreless the rest of the way with Luke Weaver (4-1) striking out Jordan Walker to get Pittsburgh out of a jam in the top of the eighth inning. St. Louis had runners on first and second on one-out singles by JJ Wetherholt and Herrera. Wetherholt led the Cardinals at the plate with two hits, including a double. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pesquisa que indicou Flávio com 50% e Lula com 21% se referia apenas a SC
item.description: Uma pesquisa que indicou o senador e candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) com 50% das intenções de voto e o presidente e postulante à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) com 21,1% era restrita a Santa Catarina, mas posts nas redes sociais compartilham o resultado como se fosse nacional.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Uma pesquisa que indicou o senador e candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) com 50% das intenções de voto e o presidente e postulante à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) com 21,1% era restrita a Santa Catarina, mas posts nas redes sociais compartilham o resultado como se fosse nacional. "Nessa pesquisa eu acredito", dizem os posts, que circulam no Facebook . O conteúdo mostra um gráfico creditado à Jovem Pan News com o título "Presidência da República" e os seguintes percentuais: Flávio Bolsonaro - 50% Lula - 21,1% Romeu Zema (Novo) - 7,5% Renan Santos (Missão) - 5,2% Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) - 4,1% Branco/Nulo - 5,4% Não sabe - 6,8% Os posts omitem, porém, que a pesquisa entrevistou somente eleitores de Santa Catarina, e não de todo o país. O mesmo gráfico foi publicado pela Jovem Pan News Florianópolis no Instagram em 12 de junho deste ano, mas com uma observação que dizia "pesquisa de cenário em Santa Catarina" -- parte cortada nas publicações checadas. "O senador Flávio Bolsonaro lidera com ampla vantagem a corrida presidencial em Santa Catarina, segundo novo levantamento do Instituto MAPA, contratado pela Jovem Pan Floripa e Jovem Pan News", afirma a legenda. O conteúdo também informa que o levantamento ocorreu entre os dias 8 e 11 de junho, ouviu 1.008 eleitores em 53 municípios catarinenses e tinha margem de erro de 3,1 pontos percentuais. Pesquisas nacionais têm apontado para uma disputa muito mais acirrada entre Lula e Flávio. Em um levantamento da Atlas/Bloomberg divulgado nesta quarta-feira, por exemplo, o presidente tinha 45,8% das intenções de voto no primeiro turno, contra 43,4% para o senador. Parte dos posts verificados ainda reproduz junto à pesquisa restrita a Santa Catarina um vídeo em que os jornalistas Julia Dualibi e Octavio Guedes, da GloboNews, comentam a queda na avaliação positiva do governo Lula para 24%, medida pelo Datafolha em fevereiro do ano passado . Na pesquisa divulgada pelo instituto na semana passada, 34% dos entrevistados avaliaram o governo Lula como ótimo ou bom. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: Nombran presidente de conglomerado energético colombiano Ecopetrol a Joaquín Gutiérrez
item.description: La junta directiva del grupo energético colombiano Ecopetrol nombró el jueves a Joaquín Gutiérrez como presidente del conglomerado que más recursos aporta al Gobierno, informó la empresa, en una de las decisiones clave de la reactivación económica y de la actividad del sector de hidrocarburos del país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La junta directiva del grupo energético colombiano Ecopetrol nombró el jueves a Joaquín Gutiérrez como presidente del conglomerado que más recursos aporta al Gobierno, informó la empresa, en una de las decisiones clave de la reactivación económica y de la actividad del sector de hidrocarburos del país. Gutiérrez, quien fue jefe de campaña del presidente Abelardo De La Espriella, asumirá el cargo en propiedad a partir del lunes 28 de septiembre. "La designación se produjo (...) para seleccionar a un líder con una capacidad excepcional de articulación que tendrá la responsabilidad de asumir el control de Ecopetrol y de esta manera iniciar una nueva etapa en una coyuntura que es especialmente retadora para la compañía", precisó un comunicado de Ecopetrol. "Los objetivos que persigue el nuevo presidente de Ecopetrol están orientados al renacimiento de la compañía desarrollando soluciones que fortalezcan su generación de valor, la realización de una gestión rigurosa y transparente y la articulación y conexión con el Estado, las comunidades, los inversionistas, los trabajadores y sus demás grupos de interés", explicó. El nuevo presidente de Ecopetrol es administrador de empresas y cuenta con tres especializaciones en gerencia de proyectos de las telecomunicaciones, derecho de las telecomunicaciones y gerencia en servicios de salud, con más de 30 años de experiencia laboral. Además, es dueño de una constructora de proyectos inmobiliarios de lujo en Bogotá y tiene inversiones en el sector salud a través de la clínica Santa Mónica en Barranquilla. De La Espriella tiene previsto el viernes un acto en la caribeña ciudad de Santa Marta denominado "Ceremonia del Renacer de Ecopetrol", en el que se espera la presentación oficial del nuevo presidente del grupo energético. Gutiérrez reemplazará a Ricardo Roa, quien renunció a finales de julio y está vinculado a una investigación como presunto responsable del delito de violación de límites de gastos en la campaña electoral que llevó al poder al expresidente Gustavo Petro en 2022. Roa también enfrenta otro proceso relacionado con un posible tráfico de influencias por la compra de un apartamento a una persona a la que después le adjudicó un contrato en un proyecto de gas. De La Espriella, un político de derecha que venció por un estrecho margen al candidato de izquierda Iván Cepeda en la segunda vuelta presidencial, prometió en su discurso de posesión reactivar el sector petrolero, estratégico para las finanzas públicas y la economía colombiana, sin dejar de lado el desarrollo de energías limpias como la solar y la eólica. También se comprometió a recuperar la solidez de Ecopetrol para aumentar las reservas y asegurar el abastecimiento de petróleo y gas, así como a impulsar la exploración y producción de hidrocarburos, lo que incluye el desarrollo del fracking responsable y sostenible. Gutiérrez asumirá el liderazgo de Ecopetrol con el reto de fortalecer la producción de hidrocarburos, garantizar la estabilidad financiera de la compañía y avanzar en proyectos de transición energética, en momentos en que el país busca atraer inversión y recuperar la confianza del sector privado. Ecopetrol, controlada en un 88,5% por el Estado colombiano, es la empresa más grande de Colombia, genera la mayor parte de la producción de petróleo del país sudamericano y es propietaria de las dos principales refinerías, así como de la mayor parte de la red de oleoductos y poliductos. La producción de Ecopetrol al cierre del primer semestre de 2026 se ubicó en 715.500 barriles de petróleo equivalente por día, una caída de 4,7% en comparación con el mismo periodo del año pasado.

item.title: 米30年債利回りが5.45%超え、20年超ぶり高水準 インフレ懸念で
item.description:
Amanda Cooper Sophie Kiderlin
[ロンドン ２４日 ロイター] - 米３０年債利回りが２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米30年債利回りが5.45%超え、20年超ぶり高水準　インフレ懸念で 4:36 配信

米国財務省入口。２月撮影。REUTERS/Ken Cedeno

Amanda Cooper　Sophie Kiderlin

[ロンドン　２４日　ロイター] - 米３０年債利回りが２４日、一時５．４５％をわずかに上回る水準まで上昇し、２００４年以来、２０年超ぶりの高水準を付けた。堅調な経済成長や高水準の債務、インフレ懸念を一段と強めるエネルギー価格の上昇を背景に、投資家が国債保有に対しより高い利回りを求める中、売りが拡大している。

指標となる１０年債利回りは５．１５８％となっている。

米国の３０年固定住宅ローン金利は戦争前と比べ１％ポイント上昇し、足元では７％と過去約２年間で最も高い水準にある。住宅ローン金利は米国債利回りに連動する。

イラン戦争によるエネルギー価格の高騰や、政府支出を巡る懸念が強まる中、債券市場は数カ月にわたって圧力にさらされており、利回りは数十年ぶりの高水準に達している。

大和キャピタル・マーケッツの経済調査責任者、クリス・シクルナ氏は「金利が上昇するほど全体の見通しが悪化するのは明らかだ。米国の住宅ローン金利はより高くなり、連邦政府の債務利払い負担も一層大きくなる」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：世界のディーゼル価格が過去最高、主要生産国の輸出急減　一段高も 焦点：トランプ氏の金利1％論、政権周辺でも異論　物価高批判そらす狙いか アングル：ＮＡＴＯが問われる「次の戦争」への備え、ドローン時代の適応に課題 アングル：「チャイナプラスワン」に逆流の兆し、中国回帰を選ぶメーカーの事情 コラム：何が豪ドルを動かしているのか＝高島修氏 最終更新: 9/25(金) 4:36 ロイター

item.title: Oracle invoca “força maior” em projeto de data center nos EUA, diz fonte
item.description: A Oracle emitiu uma notificação de “força maior” a uma unidade da Blue Owl , desenvolvedora de um grande data center no estado norte-americano do Novo México, citando possíveis atrasos no fornecimento de energia para o projeto, informou uma fonte a par do assunto à Reuters nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Isla Binnie, Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: A Oracle (ORCL.N) emitiu uma notificação de “força maior” a uma unidade da Blue Owl (OWL.N) , desenvolvedora de um grande data center no estado norte-americano do Novo México, citando possíveis atrasos no fornecimento de energia para o projeto, informou uma fonte a par do assunto à Reuters nesta quinta-feira. As ações da Oracle caíam 3,3%. A fonte afirmou que garantir o fornecimento de energia para o local é de responsabilidade da Oracle, conforme previsto no contrato. A Oracle não pode rescindir o contrato de locação sob nenhuma circunstância, disse a fonte, acrescentando que a gestora de ativos alternativos Blue Owl possui cerca de US$3 bilhões em capital próprio no projeto, sendo a Oracle responsável pelo pagamento dos custos da dívida. As empresas costumam invocar força maior para se isentar de obrigações contratuais quando surgem problemas fora de seu controle, uma medida que pode gerar preocupações entre credores e investidores. Em vez de sair como locatária principal, a Oracle está tentando adiar os pagamentos caso o data center, chamado de Projeto Júpiter, sofra atrasos e não entre em operação em 2028, conforme planejado, de acordo com uma reportagem da Bloomberg. A Oracle não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário da Reuters. “O Projeto Júpiter continua dentro do cronograma planejado”, afirmou a empresa no início do dia. A Blue Owl, proprietária da Stack Infrastructure, desenvolvedora da central de processamento de dados, afirmou que a notificação não altera os compromissos financeiros com esse projeto plurianual. Durante a fase de desenvolvimento, a Blue Owl obtém um rendimento de 9% sobre seu capital próprio, disse a fonte, acrescentando que, após a conclusão do projeto, o rendimento alavancado deverá ficar em torno de 11%. Ao invocar força maior, a Oracle prorroga o período durante o qual paga à Blue Owl o aluguel mais baixo da fase de desenvolvimento. A Blue Owl ainda receberá o aluguel mais alto pelo prazo originalmente planejado, mas o início desse pagamento será adiado, segundo a fonte. O campus do Projeto Júpiter, com cerca de 570 hectares e que garantiu US$18 bilhões em empréstimos de um consórcio de bancos, segundo reportagens da mídia, faz parte de um acordo mais amplo da Oracle com a OpenAI para fornecer capacidade de computação em IA. O campus do data center enfrenta vários contratempos de infraestrutura, incluindo atrasos na construção de um gasoduto e contestação judicial em relação a licenças relacionadas à água e à qualidade do ar. O projeto faz parte do Stargate, uma iniciativa para construir infraestrutura de IA nos EUA sob um compromisso de investimento de US$500 bilhões envolvendo OpenAI, SoftBank Group (9984.T) e parceiros, incluindo a Oracle. A construção dessa infraestrutura de IA em grande escala tem enfrentado desafios crescentes, à medida que os desenvolvedores correm para garantir energia e outros recursos, ao mesmo tempo em que gerenciam os enormes custos da implantação de capacidade computacional para parceiros como a OpenAI. A crescente oposição do público norte-americano transformou os data centers em um ponto nevrálgico político, com comunidades próximas aos projetos de centrais de processamento de dados manifestando preocupações quanto ao impacto sobre o abastecimento local de energia, água e outros recursos naturais. A corretora William Blair afirmou que, embora essa notícia intensifique as preocupações com atrasos regulatórios e relacionados ao fornecimento de energia que afetam as implantações de IA, ela espera um impacto mínimo no curto prazo para a Oracle. “Na prática, o ano fiscal de 2027 não deve ser afetado, já que o Jupiter não gera receita neste ano.”

item.title: ＵＡＥとオマーンがイラン航空便停止、米制裁受け
item.description:
Federico Maccioni Eman Abouhassira Timour Azhari
[ドバイ／リヤド ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Federico Maccioni　Eman Abouhassira　Timour Azhari

[ドバイ／リヤド ２４日 ロイター] - アラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）やオマーンを含むイラン周辺国は２４日、イラン航空会社の運航を停止した。イランとの取引がある第三国の企業を標的にするという米国の政策転換の影響が表面化した形だ。

中東最大の航空ハブであるＵＡＥの民間航空総局は、米国の新たな政策を受け、追って通知するまでイラン航空会社の全便を停止すると発表した。

イランの半国営タスニム通信によると、オマーンやジョージア、アゼルバイジャン、およびイラク首都バグダッドへの便も停止された。当局は、シーア派イスラム教徒の主要な巡礼地であるイラクのナジャフの別の空港に便を振り替える方向で調整していると伝えた。

湾岸地域の他の国もイラン便を制限したもようだ。

イランは、米国が主導する空の封鎖の履行が、緊張激化につながる恐れがあると示唆してきた。２３日には、イラン国家安全保障最高評議会のモフセン・レザイ書記が、周辺国が米国に協力してイラン便の運航を停止させれば、イランはそれらの国の空港が機能しないようにすると述べた。

item.title: ネタニヤフ氏、国連演説でイスラエル擁護 退席者やＮＹ市長を非難
item.description: [国連 ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連 ２４日 ロイター] - イスラエルのネタニヤフ首相は２４日、国連総会の一般討論演説で、中東地域におけるイスラエルの行動を擁護した。トランプ米大統領については「これ以上のパートナーはいない」と述べ、謝意を示した。

イスラエル軍によるパレスチナ自治区ガザへの攻撃を受け、国際的な孤立が深まる中、ネタニヤフ首相が演壇に立つと、会場にいた多数の外交官や各国代表が抗議の意思を示して退席した。同首相は退席者を「道徳的な臆病者」と非難し、「イスラエルは、まさにこの場を去った国々の多くを守っている」と主張した。

演説では、イスラエルの安全保障を巡り「われわれは勝つ。ほかに選択肢はない」と述べ、国家防衛を継続する姿勢を強調した。

また、自身を「戦争犯罪者」と呼んだニューヨーク市のマムダニ市長を非難し、パレスチナのイスラム組織ハマスの戦闘員を支援していると主張。さらに、欧州の指導者らが「反ユダヤ主義の暴徒」に屈したと批判したほか、カタールとトルコがイスラエルに関する虚偽の情報を広めていると非難した。

マムダニ市長については、「私がここに来るのを止めようとした。私を黙らせようとした。しかし、私を黙らせることはできない。真実を黙らせることはできない」とし、「単純な真実がある。イスラエルはジェノサイド（集団虐殺）を行っていない。イスラエルはジェノサイドを防いだのだ」と主張した。

さらに、「わが国と勇敢な兵士たちについてうそを広めている者たち、この議場にいる者であれ、反ユダヤ主義的なニューヨーク市長の事務所にいる者であれ、私はこう言いたい。恥を知れ」と述べた。

ネタニヤフ氏の苦戦が予想されるイスラエル総選挙まで５週間を切る中、ネタニヤフ首相の演説は約４０分に及び、選挙運動を思わせる内容となった。

また、トランプ大統領への謝意を示したものの、今回の訪米でトランプ大統領との首脳会談は予定されていない。

こうした中、ニューヨークの国連本部周辺には数百人の抗議者が集まり、「イスラエルへの武器供与をやめろ」などと叫んだほか、道路を封鎖するなどして警察に拘束された。

item.title: ホルムズ海峡通過船、23日は約60隻に急増＝米当局者
item.description: [ワシントン ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン　２４日　ロイター] - 米国とイランの戦争が続く中、２３日に約６０隻の商業船がホルムズ海峡を通過し、前日２２日の３隻から大幅に増加したことが分かった。また、原油の１日当たり輸送量は７月上旬以降で最大となった。米当局者がロイターに匿名を条件に明らかにした。

同当局者によると、２３日に通過した約６０隻のうち、約４０隻は米軍と連携して護衛を受けていたという。ホルムズ海峡を通過した原油は合計で約２２００万バレルに上った。

ロイターは、同当局者が示した数値を独自に確認することはできなかった。

海運データ（速報値）によると、前日２２日にホルムズ海峡を通過したコモディティー（商品）輸送船はわずか３隻と、前日の４隻から減少し、１０日移動平均の約１５隻を下回っていた。

ロイターは２４日、関係筋の話として、米国とイランがニューヨークで続けている協議で、イランがホルムズ海峡を開放し、米国が対イラン経済封鎖を解除するという、段階的な戦闘終結への道筋が模索されていると報じた。

item.title: Colombia's Ecopetrol taps presidential ally as CEO
item.description: Colombia's state-controlled oil company Ecopetrol tapped businessman Joaquin Gutierrez as chief executive, the company said on Thursday, giving one of the country's most important corporate jobs to a close presidential ally with no known background in the energy sector.
item.dc:creator: Nelson Bocanegra
item.content:encoded: Colombia's state-controlled oil company Ecopetrol (ECOPETROL.CN) tapped businessman Joaquin Gutierrez as chief executive, the company said on Thursday, giving one of the country's most important corporate jobs to a close presidential ally with no known background in the energy sector. Gutierrez, a former campaign manager for President Abelardo De La Espriella with no known track record in oil and gas, takes over as Ecopetrol faces pressure to raise output and replenish reserves. Gutierrez replaces [USN:S0N3YD03O TEXT:"Ricardo Roa"], who resigned amid investigations into campaign finance irregularities in the 2022 election and a separate influence-peddling probe linked to a gas contract. Gutierrez, a business administrator with a specialization in health management, has been described by media as a longtime confidant of De La Espriella. He has been linked to luxury real estate projects in Bogota and to healthcare investments in the Caribbean city of Barranquilla. De La Espriella has [USN:L6N4420WW TEXT:"promised to strengthen Ecopetrol"], boost reserves and [USN:L6N45G13M TEXT:"secure domestic oil and gas supply"], including through fracking. Ecopetrol, 88.49% owned by the state, is Colombia's biggest company. It accounts for most of the country's crude production and owns the Barrancabermeja and Cartagena refineries, while subsidiary Cenit controls most of the national oil and fuel pipeline network. Gutierrez takes over at a critical moment for Ecopetrol, with the company under pressure to raise oil and gas output, shore up its finances and push ahead with its energy transition plans as Colombia seeks to revive investment and restore business confidence. The company's [USN:L1N44014K TEXT:"output fell"] to an average 715,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in the first half of 2026.

item.title: Nyrstar launches strategic review of Dutch zinc smelting operations
item.description: Nyrstar, owned by commodities group Trafigura, has launched a strategic review of its loss-making Budel zinc smelting operations in the Netherlands due to r
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Nyrstar, owned by commodities group Trafigura, has launched a strategic review of its loss-making Budel zinc smelting operations in the Netherlands due to rising energy costs and government policies, it said on Thursday. Operations to produce the metal mainly used to galvanise steel will continue as normal during the review, which is expected to conclude by the end of 2026, Nyrstar added in a statement. “Nyrstar Budel faces significant pressure in terms of tough market conditions, elevated energy prices and historically low treatment and refining charges over a sustained period,” said CEO Guido Janssen. “The operation is losing money every year and the conditions for next year look particularly difficult, given rising energy costs, together with a lack of supportive government policy.” Adding to the pressure was a decision by the Dutch government not to include provisions for grid cost mitigation for energy-intensive industries in its 2027 budget, Nyrstar said. The Budel smelter, with a capacity to produce 315,000 metric tons per year of zinc, was suspended in the second half of January 2024 due to high energy costs and restarted in May of that year. “This is a significant decision point for Budel. The review will allow us to carefully assess the site’s position and the options available, while continuing to consider whether concrete action can materially improve the business case,” Janssen said. (Reporting by Eric Onstad; Editing by Susan Fenton)

item.title: Houthis say they attacked Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu
item.description: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Thursday that they had launched missile and drone attacks on what they described as "a sensitive target" in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and on Saudi Aramco facilities in the Red Sea city of Yanbu.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Thursday that they had launched missile and drone attacks on what they described as "a sensitive target" in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and on Saudi Aramco facilities in the Red Sea city of Yanbu. The statement came after Saudi Arabia said it had [USN:L1N45G0BD TEXT:"intercepted"] six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis towards the southern province of Taif and Yanbu area on the Red Sea. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of an attack on Riyadh or of damage or casualties in either Taif and Yanbu.

item.title: Bank of Mexico holds interest rate, drops signal of prolonged pause
item.description: The Bank of Mexico on Thursday held its benchmark interest rate steady at 6.50% as expected, though it dropped guidance that explicitly suggested policymakers would continue to keep borrowing costs at that level going forward.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Mexico on Thursday held its benchmark interest rate steady at 6.50% as expected, though it dropped guidance that explicitly suggested policymakers would continue to keep borrowing costs at that level going forward. The five‑member board of Banxico, as the Mexican central bank is known, was unanimous in its decision. Banxico said it would make future policy decisions by considering the ongoing disinflation process and the behavior of its determinants, including the exchange rate pass-through to consumer prices, the slack conditions and inflation expectations. The new monetary policy statement omitted language from the previous three statements which said that going forward the board estimated it would be appropriate to maintain the key interest rate at current levels. Banxico maintained its expectation that headline inflation will converge to its 3% target in the fourth quarter of 2027 and said the balance of risks for inflation remains biased to the upside. The bank pointed to uncertainty stemming from US economic policy and geopolitical conflicts, while noting that economic slack is expected to continue throughout the forecast horizon and that downside risks to economic activity persist. Economists [USN:L6N45D0CV TEXT:"polled by Reuters"] had widely expected the bank to keep rates on hold. The US Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points at its September meeting, but Banxico emphasized that Mexican monetary policy does not automatically need to follow the Fed's moves.

item.title: Oracle triggers ‘force majeure’ on data centre project over power delays, source says
item.description: Oracle issued a “force majeure” notice to a Blue Owl unit, developer of a large New Mexico data centre, citing delays in securing power for the project.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: Oracle issued a “force majeure” notice to a Blue Owl unit, the developer of a large New Mexico data centre, citing potential delays in securing power for the project, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday. Shares of Oracle fell around four per cent. The source said that securing power for the site is Oracle’s responsibility under the contract. Oracle cannot terminate the lease under any circumstances, the source said, adding that alternative asset manager Blue Owl has about US$3 billion in equity in the project, with Oracle responsible for paying the debt costs. Companies typically invoke force majeure to free themselves from contractual obligations when problems arise beyond their control, a move that can raise concerns among lenders and investors. Rather than exiting as the main tenant, Oracle is attempting to delay payments should the data centre dubbed Project Jupiter get derailed and fail to come online in 2028 as planned, according to a report by Bloomberg News, which first reported the development. Oracle did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. “Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule,” the company said earlier in the day. Blue Owl, which owns the data-centre developer Stack Infrastructure, said the notice does not change the financial commitments to this multi-year project. During the development stage, Blue Owl earns a nine per cent yield on its equity, the source said, adding that upon completion of the project, the levered yield is expected to be around 11 per cent. By invoking force majeure, Oracle extends the period during which it pays Blue Owl the lower development-stage rent. Blue Owl will still receive the higher rent for the originally planned duration, but its start will be delayed, according to the source. The 1,400-acre Project Jupiter campus, which secured US$18 billion in loans from a consortium of banks, according to media reports, is part of Oracle’s broader agreement with OpenAI to provide AI computing capacity. The data centre campus has reportedly faced multiple infrastructure setbacks, including delays to a planned natural-gas pipeline and legal challenges over water and air-quality permits. The project is a part of Stargate, an initiative to build AI infrastructure in the US under a US$500 billion investment commitment involving OpenAI, SoftBank Group 9984.T and partners including Oracle. The massive AI infrastructure build-out has faced mounting challenges, as developers race to secure power, water and other resources while managing the enormous costs of deploying computing capacity for partners such as OpenAI. Growing opposition from the public has made data centres a political flashpoint, with communities around data centre projects raising concerns over their impact on local supply of energy, water and other natural resources. Brokerage William Blair said while this news intensifies worries about regulatory and power-related delays affecting AI deployments, it expects minimal short-term impact on Oracle. “Practically, fiscal 2027 should not be affected, since Jupiter contributes no revenue this year.” --- Reporting by Isla Binnie and reporting by Jaspreet Singh in Bengaluru; additional reporting by Prakhar Srivastava; Editing by Devika Syamnath, Anil D’Silva and Maju Samuel

item.title: Banco central de México mantiene tasa clave; próximos pasos dependerán de la desinflación, no de la Fed
item.description: El banco central de México (Banxico) mantuvo el jueves su tasa de interés referencial en un 6.5%, como esperaba el mercado, y dijo que sus próximas decisiones se guiarán por el proceso desinflacionario, sin seguir mecánicamente los movimientos de la Reserva Federal (Fed).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El banco central de México (Banxico) mantuvo el jueves su tasa de interés referencial en un 6.5%, como esperaba el mercado, y dijo que sus próximas decisiones se guiarán por el proceso desinflacionario, sin seguir mecánicamente los movimientos de la Reserva Federal (Fed). La autoridad monetaria dejó en un 3.5% su pronóstico para la inflación general al cierre de 2026 y ajustó al alza la de la subyacente a un 3.6% desde un 3.5% previo. También conservó su expectativa para la convergencia a la meta del 3% para el cuarto trimestre del 2027. La [USN:L1N45G0FW TEXT:"inflación "]general de México se aceleró en la primera quincena de septiembre más de lo previsto, a un 3.42% interanual, mientras que el índice subyacente siguió moderándose, al ubicarse en un 3.79%, informó el instituto de estadística horas antes del anuncio. Banxico señaló que el balance de riesgos para la inflación mantiene un sesgo al alza, ante la incertidumbre por cambios en la política económica de Estados Unidos y una posible prolongación de los conflictos geopolíticos, que podrían generar presiones inflacionarias. "Hacia delante, la Junta de Gobierno tomará sus decisiones considerando la continuación del proceso desinflacionario y el comportamiento esperado de sus determinantes, incluyendo el traspaso del tipo de cambio a los precios del consumidor, las condiciones de holgura y las expectativas de inflación", dijo en su comunicado. Agregó que dado que las condiciones macroeconómicas en México son distintas a las de Estados Unidos, "la política monetaria no tendría que reaccionar de manera mecánica ante los ajustes previstos a la tasa de fondos federales". La semana pasada, [USN:L1N4580T6 TEXT:"la Fed "]elevó los tipos de interés en un cuarto de punto porcentual, su primera subida desde julio de 2023, y sus proyecciones apuntaron a al menos otro incremento antes de que acabe el año. Analistas destacaron el comentario de Banxico desligando sus decisiones de la autoridad monetaria estadounidense. "Lo más importante es que la Junta destacó que México y Estados Unidos se encuentran en etapas diferentes del ciclo económico, lo que otorga a Banxico margen para fijar su política en función de las condiciones internas", dijo Andrés Abadía, economista jefe para América Latina de Pantheon Macroeconomics.

item.title: Trump-Xi summit in Washington begins with great fanfare but low expectations
item.description: “We had a great meeting,” US President Donald Trump said after a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, earlier hailing a “truly great friendship” with the Chinese leader.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Trump-Xi summit in Washington begins with great fanfare but low expectations

“We had a great meeting,” US President Donald Trump said after a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, earlier hailing a “truly great friendship” with the Chinese leader.

US President Donald Trump, right, China's President Xi Jinping watch a silent drill platoon review on the new helipad from the Blue Room Balcony of the White House, Thursday, Sep 24, 2026, in Washington. (Photo: AP/Alex Brandon)

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday (Sep 24) for a lavish state summit expected to be heavy on symbolism but light on substance, with both leaders keen to showcase stable ties despite a host of thorny issues such as AI, trade, Taiwan and the war with Iran. The subject of Taiwan, perhaps the most difficult, came up during a bilateral meeting in which Xi urged the US to oppose "Taiwan independence," according to a readout from the official Chinese news agency Xinhua shortly after it concluded. The White House did not immediately provide its own readout of the discussion. Xi had been expected to press Trump this week to halt arms sales to Taiwan. Following his visit to China in May, Trump said he was holding in abeyance an arms package to Taiwan worth some US$14 billion and called it a "very good negotiating chip." The move left some US allies in Asia and even some of Trump's fellow Republicans concerned that he may be tempted to soften Washington's support for Taipei in exchange for economic wins with China. China has long asserted territorial ownership of Taiwan, a democratically governed island that relies on US power to counter Beijing's threats. Despite backing Taiwan, the US has traditionally avoided taking an official stance on the island's independence.

Earlier on Thursday at the White House , Trump touted his "truly great friendship" with Xi and said the two powers had made strides on trade since his trip to China in May . "During this visit, we will also discuss pressing issues concerning security, technology, and 'super intelligence,'" Trump said, using his alternative name for artificial intelligence . "The decisions we make in these areas today can promote peace and prosperity for decades and decades to come." Speaking after Trump, Xi said the competition between the US and China should be a "healthy one." US companies were welcome in China, he said, adding that he hopes "Chinese companies are treated fairly here in the United States." Xi also said both militaries should maintain regular dialogue to improve crisis prevention. "The Thucydides trap can be overcome," he said, referring to the academic theory that sees a risk of rivalry between a rising and an established power spiralling into open conflict. The summit, Xi's first visit to Washington in more than a decade, is the second meeting this year between the leaders of the world's two biggest economies.

POMP AND CIRCUMSTANCE For Trump, who relishes ceremony and prizes his ties with powerful leaders, the visit is as much a matter of national prestige as an opportunity for high-stakes diplomacy. The US president aimed to reciprocate the grand welcome he received in China in May. But Trump and Xi's remarks were not carried live by any US television networks, which have collectively declined to provide footage in protest of the White House's ban of CNN, MS Now and Politico . Trump greeted Xi on arrival on Wednesday evening with a red carpet on the tarmac, the first time a US president has welcomed a foreign leader at Joint Base Andrews since President Barack Obama met Pope Francis in 2015, according to C-SPAN, which tracks presidential events. Following their remarks on Thursday, the two leaders observed a military ceremony including a flyover at the Rose Garden, with Chinese flags waving from the Oval Office roof alongside US flags, before a scheduled bilateral meeting. Trump's embrace of Xi could complicate his campaign message at home ahead of November's midterm elections, when Republicans' narrow congressional majorities are at stake as voters fret about inflation and the war on Iran. The president for months has labelled Democrats "communists" in an effort to paint them as too extreme, but he welcomed Xi, the head of the Chinese Communist Party, on Thursday as a dear personal friend.

BREAKTHROUGHS UNLIKELY Despite the fanfare, analysts say major breakthroughs are unlikely, with tangible outcomes potentially limited to an extension of a trade truce expiring in November and an agreement to examine threats posed by artificial intelligence. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Wednesday after talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng that they had agreed to extend until Jan 10 an agreement that paused a trade war that saw mutual tariffs top 100%. Trump wrote in a Truth Social post on Thursday morning that the two leaders would discuss "super intelligence" but again indicated he has little interest in imposing new regulations, despite concerns from industry leaders that AI could eventually pose a threat to humans. "Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is," Trump wrote. "That is China's position also." During his comments on Thursday, Xi said both countries have "the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good, and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control." Analysts say intense competition between the two powers in AI is likely to limit the scope for anything beyond symbolic agreements.

Related:

CNN, MS NOW, Politico allowed back in White House after judge's order

Trump’s high-level welcome for Xi puts personal diplomacy in focus, analysts say

KEEPING TIES STABLE People familiar with the plans say the talks could also yield deals to lower some tariffs, combat drug trafficking and expand military-to-military dialogue, while Trump is expected to seek the release of Americans and others detained in China. Xi appears to be in a stronger position, having overseen a surge in China's trade and firmly in control of supplies of rare earth minerals that give him powerful leverage. Both leaders see advantages in keeping relations stable, with Trump mired in the unpopular Iran war and Xi grappling with domestic economic challenges. But beneath the surface are challenges that could reignite tensions, including disputes over Taiwan, export controls and AI. The leaders will likely discuss the Iran war, but there has been little sign Beijing is willing to exert pressure on its ally to yield to US demands. The guest list for Thursday's state dinne r includes CEOs like Apple's Tim Cook, Amazon's Jeff Bezos, Alphabet's Sundar Pichai, OpenAI's Sam Altman, Tesla's Elon Musk and Nvidia's Jensen Huang, but despite such an array, people familiar with US plans say Trump is likely to maintain firm export controls on US tech Xi wants loosened.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: 米イラン、段階的停戦案を模索 ホルムズ海峡開放と封鎖解除が軸＝関係筋
item.description:
Samia Nakhoul Parisa Hafezi John Irish
[２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Samia Nakhoul　Parisa Hafezi　John Irish

[２４日 ロイター] - 米国とイランがニューヨークで続けている協議で、イランがホルムズ海峡を開放し、米国が対イラン経済封鎖を解除するという、段階的な戦闘終結への道筋が模索されていることが複数の関係筋の話で分かった。

原油輸送の要衝であるホルムズ海峡は、開始から約７カ月が経過した米イラン紛争の終結に向けた交渉の中心的な争点になっているが、イランも米国も交渉上の切り札を先に手放すことを望んでいないため、協議は大きな障害に直面している。ただ、イラン関係筋２人、中東地域の当局者２人、西側外交筋２人はロイターに対し、イランは対立の長期化がもたらす経済的代償も認識していると明らかにした。

イラン高官は、行き詰まりを打開する最も現実的な方法は段階的な取り決めになると指摘。イランがホルムズ海峡での航行を認める見返りとして、米国が経済封鎖を解除し、イランが凍結資産へのアクセスを回復する可能性もあるという。この高官は国連総会の会場で「危機を段階的に解決することが前進への道になり得る。まず封鎖を終わらせ、ホルムズ海峡を開放することだ」と述べた。

こうした案を実現させるには、７月に崩壊した従来の合意に続く新たな暫定的な取り決めをトランプ米大統領が受け入れる必要がある。

トランプ大統領は、１１月３日の中間選挙後に米国とイランが合意に達する可能性があるとの見方を示しているが、欧州の高官はイランには「非常に長い要求リスト」があると指摘。米ホワイトハウス当局者は「イランは合意を切望しているが、トランプ大統領が主導権を握っており、米国にとって最善の決定を下す」とした上で、トランプ氏は「適切な条件の下」でイランとの対話には前向きだが、交渉を急ぐ必要はないとの考えを示していると語った。

item.title: MercadoLibre launches deliveries within an hour, expands pharmacy business in Brazil
item.description: MercadoLibre launched product deliveries within an hour in Brazil, starting in the city of Sao Paulo, Fernando Yunes, the firm's executive vice president of commerce, said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: MercadoLibre (MELI.O) launched product deliveries within an hour in Brazil, starting in the city of Sao Paulo, Fernando Yunes, the firm's executive vice president of commerce, said on Thursday. The Latin American e-commerce and fintech company also will expand its pharmacy business in the country, with its own pharmacy in Sao Paulo beginning to sell prescription products this month, Yunes said at a company event. MercadoLibre will add third-party pharmacies to its e-commerce platform in Brazil as of October, kicking off in Sao Paulo with three drugstore chains, which were not named. The company expects to have 20 third-party physical drugstore locations in Sao Paulo on its platform by the end of the year. The one-hour service, which started as a test in an undisclosed region of Sao Paulo and is expected to be expanded, will include products such as medications, food and others.

item.title: US Federal Reserve proposes new stablecoin rules
item.description: The US Federal Reserve on Thursday proposed new rules for issuers of dollar-backed cryptocurrency tokens known as stablecoins, as required by last year's GENIUS Act, which established a federal regulatory framework for the tokens.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Lang
item.content:encoded: The US Federal Reserve on Thursday proposed new rules for issuers of dollar-backed cryptocurrency tokens known as stablecoins, as required by [USN:L1N3T70SB TEXT:"last year's GENIUS Act"], which established a federal regulatory framework for the tokens. Under the proposal, the Fed would require that payment stablecoin issuers under its supervision fully back their tokens with certain reserve assets, such as short-term Treasury bills The proposal would also impose capital requirements on stablecoin issuers to address certain credit and operational risks If enacted, the new rules would introduce guidelines for Fed-supervised banks that custody reserves on behalf of stablecoin issuers The proposal would also outline stablecoin-related activities Fed-supervised banks can engage in, and would establish a tailored application process for banks that want to issue their own stablecoins The Fed will accept comment on the proposed new rules for 60 days after they are published in the Federal Register

item.title: Alaska Air expects Boeing 737 MAX 10 certification this month
item.description: Alaska Air expects Boeing's 737 MAX 10 to be certified by the end of September and plans to take delivery of its first aircraft next spring, Chief Operating Officer Jason Berry told Reuters on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole, Rajesh Singh
item.content:encoded: Alaska Air (ALK.N) expects Boeing's (BA.N) 737 MAX 10 to be certified by the end of September and plans to take delivery of its first aircraft next spring, Chief Operating Officer Jason Berry told Reuters on Thursday. The airline expects to put the MAX 10 into passenger service between April and mid-May, Berry said. The Federal Aviation Administration must certify the MAX 10, whose approval has already been delayed for years, before Boeing can begin deliveries. Any further delay could put pressure on Alaska's planned timetable for introducing the jet. Berry said Alaska would still need to complete certification work related to the head-up display used by pilots after the aircraft itself is approved, a process he said would take a "few months." The tight timeline "is sporting," he said, adding that "we're not panicking yet." Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said last week that certification of the 737-10 was coming "very soon." Flight testing has been completed and Boeing is working through final documentation with the FAA. Boeing declined to comment further on Thursday. ALASKA GROWTH PLANS Certification is an important milestone for Boeing's financial recovery. The MAX 10, the largest version of the 737 MAX family, accounted for about 31% of Boeing's undelivered 737 orders at the end of June. Alaska has also made the aircraft a major part of its growth plans. Berry said the carrier now expects 22 MAX 10 deliveries in 2027 and 30 in 2028. In January, Alaska placed the [USN:L6N3Y80SN TEXT:"largest aircraft order"] in its history, including 105 MAX 10s and rights for another 35. The larger jet will allow Alaska to add seats on busy routes such as New York and Boston without adding more flights, Berry said. Alaska currently has no plans to install lie-flat seats on the MAX 10, although Berry said that remains an option.

item.title: Yalcouye makes dream debut as Ivory Coast beat Ghana in heavyweight clash
item.description: Ivory Coast debutant Malick Yalcouye scored the first goal and won the penalty for the second as they beat neighbours Ghana 2-0 in a fiery start to Africa Cup of Nations qualifying on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gleeson
item.content:encoded: Ivory Coast debutant Malick Yalcouye scored the first goal and won the penalty for the second as they beat neighbours Ghana 2-0 in a fiery start to Africa Cup of Nations qualifying on Thursday. Captain Frank Kessie converted a 58th-minute penalty in Bouake but it was the 20-year-old Brighton & Hove Albion attacker who stole the show in his first appearance, handing the home side the lead with a powerful left footed strike from outside the penalty area one minute before halftime. Both the Ivorians and Ghanaians had got to the last-32 at the World Cup in mid-year and were playing their first game since their exploits at the tournament in Canada, Mexico and the US. The Group C encounter was the first game back in charge for coach Herve Renard, who won the Cup of Nations with Ivory Coast in 2015, and whose new-look team dominated proceedings against a Ghana side hit by injury and missing the likes of Mohamed Kudus and Antoine Semenyo. The opening day of the group qualifiers for next year’s finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda also had wins for Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mauritania, Namibia and Zimbabwe. However, Tunisia, who were the only one of 10 African teams not to advance past the first phase of the World Cup, let an early lead slip and were held 1-1 at home by Uganda as their disappointing form continued. DR Congo won 2-0 at home in Kinshasa against Equatorial Guinea with Chancel Mbemba heading in early and Yoane Wissa adding the second while also in Group E, Zimbabwe fought back from 2-0 down at halftime to beat Sierra Leone 3-2 with Marshall Munetsi (2) and Tawanda Chirewa scoring. LATE INSURANCE GOAL Cameroon debutant David Nyengue opened the scoring and Bryan Mbeumo added the second in Garoua but they had to sweat it out for a 3-1 triumph after tiny Comoros pulled one back through Bundesliga-based Warmed Omari. Cameroon got a late insurance goal from English-born Daniel Namasso. Libya netted a last-gasp penalty to salvage a 2-2 draw at home to Botswana behind closed doors in Tripoli, where there was a stadium ban because of previous supporter violence. Botswana striker Tumisang Orebonye scored a double in the first half to put his side on course for a rare away win before Maruwan Alhibeeshi thrashed home from the edge of the area to pull one back in the 87th minute. Botswana substitute Mothusi Cooper gave away a stoppage-time penalty with a clumsy challenge, allowing Ezoo El Mariamy to rescue a draw. Mauritania won 3-1 over the Central African Republic in Casablanca, Morocco, which included a superb chipped effort over the goalkeeper from Dawda Camara, while Betuel Muzeu scored the only goal as Namibia edged Congo.

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（24日）
item.description:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞
続落して取引を終えた。原油先物価格の上昇を受けて、インフレ懸念が高まった。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は３...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（24日） 3:37 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

続落して取引を終えた。原油先物価格の上昇を受けて、インフレ懸念が高まった。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は３日連続で下落。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．８５％安だった。

米・イランの戦闘終結に向けた協議に大きな進展の兆しが見られない中、原油価格が上昇。英１０年債利回りは一時５．３８％を付けた。

石油大手のＢＰは２．６％、シェルは１．７％それぞれ上昇した。

一方、エンジンメーカーのロールスロイスは１．３％、防衛大手ＢＡＥシステムズは１．５％、いずれも下落。利益見通しを下方修正した住宅建設のビストリー・グループは３．１％値下がりした。保険のスタンダード・ライフは４．２％、テクノロジー・サービスプロバイダーのコンピュータセンターは４．４％、それぞれ下落した。

イングランド銀行（英中銀）の副総裁２人は今後の利上げの可能性を示唆。金融政策委員会の１人の委員はインフレリスクを判断する上で冬場の動向が鍵になるとの見方を示した。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

続落して取引を終えた。原油価格の上昇を受けてユーロ圏の債券利回りが高水準で推移し、投資家にリスクを回避する姿勢が強まった。主要な地域指数も大半がマイナス圏だった。

米イランの交渉に進展の兆しが見られず、ブレント原油先物価格は１バレル＝１００ドルを上回る水準で取引された。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種テクノロジー株指数は１．６０％、工業株指数は１．４２％、ヘルスケア株指数は０．１４％、いずれも下落した。

直近の四半期決算を発表したスウェーデンのファストファッション大手Ｈ＆Ｍは２．０％安だった。

一方、石油・ガス株指数は１．１２％高。食品・飲料株指数は０．７０％、個人・家庭用品株指数は０．２１％それぞれ上昇した。

米中首脳会談に関心が集まる中、ベセント米財務長官は２３日、米中が「貿易休戦」の延長で合意したと明らかにした。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

域内国債利回りが上昇した。原油価格の再上昇に加え、堅調な企業活動指標を受けて欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）による追加金融引き締めの観測が強まった。

ユーロ圏の指標となるドイツ１０年債利回りは１７年超ぶりの高水準となる３．５７９８％まで上昇。終盤では３ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇となった。

堅調な経済指標も債券売りに拍車をかけた。独ＩＦＯ経済研究所が２４日発表した９月の業況指数は８９．９と、前月の８８．８から上昇し、市場予想を上回った。nL6N45G0JX

短期金融市場の先物は、ＥＣＢが年末までに約３５ｂｐの引き締めを行うことを織り込んでおり、これは０．２５％ポイントの利上げ１回と、２回目の利上げ確率が約４０％であることを意味する。先物は今後１２カ月間に０．２５％ポイントの利上げが４回行われることを織り込んでいる。

ドイツ２年債利回りは横ばいの３．２８４％。

フランス１０年債利回りは一時、１８年超ぶりの高水準となる４．６９６％まで上昇した。

仏独１０年債の利回り格差は１１１ｂｐ超まで拡大し、２０１２年半ば以来の最大幅となった。スプレッドの拡大は一般に、投資家がドイツ国債と比較してフランス国債保有のリスクが高まっていると認識している兆候と見なされる。

item.title: France to send military to protect Saudi Arabia on Red Sea oil route, Macron says
item.description: France will send troops and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, which is key for energy transport, French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France will send troops and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, which is key for energy transport, French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday. Macron also said a [USN:S0N43J04J TEXT:"US ban on diesel exports"], which the White House has denied is under consideration, would be "catastrophic," both globally and for the US economy. Macron was speaking in a wide-ranging primetime television interview on the international situation, in which he also warned about possible Russian attacks on French soil. Facing growing pressure at home over high energy prices, Macron sought to assure the French that France had adequate gas and oil supplies as winter approaches. He said Paris was actively working to ensure flows were not disrupted. Crude oil prices have surged recently as the main alternative route for Saudi oil exports through Yanbu has come under missile attacks from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. "We are going to send military resources, that is to say, soldiers, radar systems and defence systems, to protect this site - not to get us involved in any conflicts, but to protect this site," Macron told TF1 and France 2 TV. RUSSIAN THREAT Macron dismissed a report by Spanish newspaper El Mundo that the US Central Intelligence Agency had warned European governments about the threat of potential drone attacks from the Mediterranean. "I can deny it. The CIA did not inform French services," he said. Still, Macron said Russia is multiplying hostile and criminal acts against European countries, and France could face strikes similar to the failed attack in Leipzig. Germany said [USN:L8N44T1N2 TEXT:"Russia was responsible"] for an attempted drone attack in August on the Leipzig airport. Macron gathered French party chiefs at the Elysee last week to brief them on the growing threat from Russia. He later said he had ordered his government to draw up a plan to protect critical infrastructure against drone and cyber attacks. Macron said Moscow was seeking to intimidate Europe and break the continent's resolve in supporting Ukraine. Russia says European allegations of hybrid attacks are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria. Yet Macron's position on Russia was weakened this week after France shocked other EU members by getting Russian-Uzbek metals tycoon Alisher Usmanov exempted from EU sanctions, citing national security concerns. That prompted Azerbaijan to pardon a French national jailed for espionage.

item.title: White House reinstates access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico following judge's order
item.description: The White House said on Thursday it has reinstated journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico after a federal judge deemed US President Donald Trump's ban of the three news outlets likely unconstitutional and ordered their access immediately restored.
item.dc:creator: Susan Heavey, Helen Coster
item.content:encoded: The White House said on Thursday it has reinstated journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico after a federal judge deemed US President Donald Trump 's [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"ban of the three news outlets"] likely unconstitutional and ordered their access immediately restored. The midday reinstatement came after a chaotic few hours earlier on Thursday when the journalists continued to be blocked from entering the White House grounds. That prompted the three news organizations to request an immediate hearing before US District Judge Tim Kelly, who issued his decision overnight. Kelly, acting in a lawsuit brought by CNN, MS NOW and Politico on Monday, ordered a halt to Trump's ban for 14 days in a press freedom case that has played out over the past week in the courtroom and White House grounds. Kelly found that the revocation of the White House credentials of the journalists "likely violated their constitutional due process rights." The judge, who Trump appointed in 2017 during his first presidential term, also raised doubts about the US Justice Department's national security arguments for justifying the ban, noting that Trump himself had said the action was due to what the president alleged was false or negative coverage. Hours after Kelly issued his order, CNN, MS NOW and Politico told the judge they remained barred, and asked for the emergency hearing. Politico said its reporter's credentials were confiscated. An MS NOW reporter said she was blocked from the White House. CNN said some of its staff members were denied entry onto the grounds. In response, Micah Stopperich, the director of press operations at the White House, said in a court filing that the White House began the process of reinstating press badges for affected reporters at 7:25 a.m., and that the "White House press team dropped badges at the entry gate for members of the press to pick up around 9:55 a.m." After receiving Stopperich's declaration, the judge denied the request by the news organizations for an emergency hearing but gave them an opportunity to inform him of any factual developments later in the day. The sharpest conflict yet between Trump and the press played out during a key diplomatic moment for the US president: his appearance at the United Nations General Assembly in New York and his hosting of Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday. A source familiar with the White House television press pool said its members would not reinstate their coverage until the White House formally reinstates CNN to the pool. Earlier this week, they had suspended pooled coverage in solidarity with CNN. There were no TV pool cameras set up for Xi's arrival on the White House's South Lawn on Thursday morning, and FOX News, MS NOW and CNN did not air the two leaders' arrival ceremony live. During Trump's welcome of Xi to the White House, the president made a joke to photographers in the Oval Office about the Chinese having the friendliest press corps. CNN is one of the five news organizations – along with ABC, CBS, FOX News and NBC – that make up the primary White House television pool. They share the costs of covering the president, take turns organizing coverage and provide footage to other outlets. CNN had been scheduled to cover Trump's trip to New York for the General Assembly on Monday, but was not able to provide a pool feed. NATIONAL SECURITY CONCERNS Trump announced the ban on Friday on his social media platform, saying those news organizations "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States." Trump framed their reporting as a threat to US national security. The three outlets sued Trump and other members of his administration, saying the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations, including Reuters, later filed a legal brief supporting the three news outlets. Kelly ordered the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets' press passes and stop enforcing the ban for two weeks. The judge rejected the administration's stated national security concerns. "The record lacks factual support for defendants' contention that the revocation of plaintiffs' hard passes will in fact protect national security or that national security will be endangered if the court orders their passes reinstated while this litigation proceeds," Kelly wrote. In a filing on Tuesday, the Justice Department accused the outlets of threatening national security with their coverage, citing stories about US missile stockpiles, construction of Trump's White House ballroom and turnout at the recent Republican midterm convention. Theodore Boutrous, an attorney for the three outlets, welcomed the judge's decision in a statement, saying: "This is a strong ruling vindicating freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law. We greatly appreciate the court's swift action." TENSIONS WITH THE PRESS Although other presidential administrations have battled with the press, Trump's campaign against the media has been unprecedented. Upending decades of tradition, his White House had denied basic access to many major news organizations, launched personal attacks on journalists and filed multiple lawsuits against news organizations. Kelly's ruling came a day after Trump experienced another legal setback. On Wednesday, an Iowa judge [USN:L4N45F1L5 TEXT:"dismissed"] Trump's 2024 lawsuit against the Des Moines Register newspaper and pollster J. Ann Selzer. Trump sued the Register, its parent company Gannett and Selzer over a poll published ahead of the November 2024 US election that showed Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris leading him in Iowa. Trump accused the newspaper and its longtime pollster of fraudulently misleading readers. In his ruling Wednesday, Iowa District Judge Scott Beattie said the poll was legally protected speech.

item.title: 英インフレリスク、冬場に顕在 早期利下げに慎重＝ディングラ中銀政策委員
item.description: [ロンドン ２４日 ロイター] - イングランド銀行（英中央銀行、ＢＯＥ）金融政策委員会（ＭＰＣ）のディングラ委員は２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
英インフレリスク、冬場に顕在　早期利下げに慎重＝ディングラ中銀政策委員 3:21 配信

２０２３年３月撮影　REUTERS/Hannah McKay

[ロンドン　２４日　ロイター] - イングランド銀行（英中央銀行、ＢＯＥ）金融政策委員会（ＭＰＣ）のディングラ委員は２４日、米イラン情勢の緊迫化に伴う原油高に伴う英国の長期的なインフレ影響は、エネルギー需要が高まる冬場に顕在化するとの見方を示した。中期的なインフレ要因も年末までに明確になり始めるとし、早期利上げには慎重な姿勢を示した。

英シンクタンクの国立経済社会研究所（ＮＩＥＳＲ） の会議に出席したディングラ氏は、冬場にかけて「賃金交渉の行方や最終的水準についても、より多くのことが分かってくる。金融引き締めはすでに進行中だ」と述べた。

一方、ロシアによるウクライナ侵攻を受けてエネルギー価格が急騰した２０２２年のような、広範囲にわたる物価上昇は起きておらず、雇用市場も弱含んでいると指摘した。欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）や米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は利上げに動いているものの、英国の需要水準は米国を下回り、指標金利もユーロ圏よりも高いため、英中銀の据え置き決定は妥当だと主張した。ディングラ氏は、今月のＭＰＣで金利据え置きを支持していた。

人工知能（ＡＩ）の利用拡大がサービス部門でのインフレ鈍化につながる可能性があるとの見方も示したほか、英国の中期的なインフレ期待は懸念すべき状況ではないとした。

また、英中銀のロンバルデリ副総裁は２４日、景気減速が鮮明にならない限り、エネルギー価格の高止まりを受けて利上げが必要になるとの認識を示した。

item.title: 約80カ国が国連で共同声明、ホルムズ海峡の再開要求 イランとフーシ派非難
item.description: [国連 ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連　２４日　ロイター] - 世界の約８０カ国は国連で２４日、ホルムズ海峡の緊急再開を求めるとともに、同地域での攻撃や国際貿易・エネルギー安全保障の混乱を巡ってイランとその同盟勢力であるイエメンの武装組織フーシ派を非難した。

バーレーンのザヤーニ外相は共同声明で「ホルムズ海峡におけるイランの行動は、国際的な安全保障および航行の権利と自由を脅かし続けている」と指摘。「またイエメンでの紛争を再開させたフーシ派の決定、サウジアラビアへの継続的な攻撃、紅海における無謀な攻撃についても強く非難する」と述べた。

また、フーシ派がバベルマンデブ海峡に向けて進軍を続けていることは、国際的な海運、海上安全保障、世界貿易に対するリスクを一段と高めるだけだと非難した。

声明には、湾岸アラブ諸国をはじめ主要な西側諸国が賛同した。

By Lili Bayer BRUSSELS, Sept 24 (Reuters) – The European Union is not rearming quickly or effectively enough to meet its goal of being ready to defend against Russia by 2030, according to the executive summary of an EU report prepared for the bloc’s leaders and seen by Reuters.

EU members’ current plans “do not seem to meet” the goal of filling gaps in areas such as air and missile defence, ground combat, naval forces, munition stockpiles and drones, the European Defence Agency said in its first annual Defence Readiness Report.

“Tackling the challenges of a contested and deteriorating security environment and the threat posed by Russia’s aggression requires moving further and substantially faster than now to reach defence readiness by 2030,” the EU agency wrote.

Show Full Article

ACHIEVEMENTS UNPRECEDENTED BUT ‘NOT YET ENOUGH’

Leaders from the EU’s 27 countries ordered the report last year to assess progress in their drive to ramp up Europe’s defences, reflecting fears fuelled by Russia’s war in Ukraine and calls by US President Donald Trump for Europe to do more for its own security.

Trump has also threatened to withdraw from the NATO alliance that has been the bedrock of European security for decades, although he recommitted to its mutual defence clause at a summit in Ankara in July.

Russia has denied it has any intention of attacking an EU member and accused the continent’s leaders of fearmongering. But EU leaders have dismissed Moscow’s assertions, pointing out it made similar comments before its 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Against such an uncertain international backdrop, EU leaders last year set themselves the goal of making Europe ready to defend itself by 2030.

EU defence ministers are expected to discuss the defence agency’s report in Brussels on Monday and it will then go to the bloc’s leaders.

“The first Annual Defence Readiness Report shows progress in spending, capability development, and industrial readiness, supported by deepened partnerships, notably with Ukraine,” the summary seen by Reuters said.

“However, the current momentum and increased investment do not yet translate into sufficiently deployable, sustainable and interoperable forces, while critical capability gaps remain. What has been achieved so far, although unprecedented, is not yet enough.”

(Reporting by Lili Bayer, editing by Andrew Gray and Andrew Heavens)

item.title: BP eyes Devon Energy asset amid renewed US M&A ambitions, sources say
item.description: BP is weighing a potential acquisition of Devon Energy's operations in South Texas as part of renewed efforts by the British supermajor to grow its shale asset base in the US, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: David French, Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: BP (BP.L) is weighing a potential acquisition of Devon Energy's (DVN.N) operations in South Texas as part of renewed efforts by the British supermajor to grow its shale asset base in the US, people familiar with the matter said. After years of prioritizing investments in renewable energy and leadership churn that included five chief executives since 2020, London-headquartered BP has reverted to a strategy that places its traditional oil and gas business at its heart. Since [USN:L6N40X0S5 TEXT:"Meg O'Neill"] joined as CEO in April, BP has entered the data room on a small number of shale assets placed for sale by their owners, allowing the company access to confidential information provided to prospective buyers so they can evaluate the merits of a deal, according to six sources. BP has targeted predominantly oil-producing assets with valuations of between $2 billion and $5 billion, three of the sources said. This includes Devon Energy's Eagle Ford asset, which opened its data room in late August, said three of the sources. Analysts at TPH Research said in a note on Wednesday the asset could be worth around $4.5 billion. The sources cautioned that entering a data room does not guarantee that BP will formally bid on an asset. They spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss private deliberations. Shares in Devon extended gains in the wake of the Reuters report, and closed 1.8% higher on Thursday. Devon has risen around 34% this year, per LSEG data. BP declined comment. Devon did not respond to a comment request. BPX ENERGY BP's US shale operations are held within its BPX Energy unit, with assets in the Eagle Ford, Permian and Haynesville basins spanning Texas and Louisiana. Production in the second quarter was around 545,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), of which its existing Eagle Ford was approximately 205,000 boepd, according to an August presentation. The company is targeting over 650,000 boepd from BPX by 2030, according to BP's website. Despite its strategic pivot back to oil and gas, previously overseen by Albert Manifold before he was fired as chair and replaced on a permanent basis earlier this month by [USN:L6N44U0DM TEXT:"Ian Tyler"], BP has spent the last 18 months focused on reducing debt and hitting a [USN:L6N4410CR TEXT:"$20 billion divestment"] target. While it has engaged in some acquisition activity in that time, including showing interest in buying a majority stake in the [USN:L6N40E0X4 TEXT:"Shenandoah field"] in the US Gulf, BP had been largely absent from shale data rooms, making its re-emergence in recent weeks as a potential buyer notable, three of the sources said. Buying assets near its existing footprint would be logical, four of the sources said, given the potential for cost savings and BP's familiarity with local geology. Part of Devon's Eagle Ford asset was held in a joint venture between the company and BP until the partnership's dissolution in 2025. DEVON DIVESTMENT Devon is marketing for sale both its Eagle Ford and Powder River basin acreage in Wyoming, the sources said, as part of a [USN:L4N4411YP TEXT:"portfolio review"] undertaken following its $58 billion merger with Coterra Energy. The Eagle Ford asset consists of around 90,000 net acres, and produced around 77,000 boepd in the second quarter, per Devon's website. The effort comes as U.S. energy assets have increased allure to buyers, as they can operate even as Middle Eastern conflict shakes global oil markets. The tension pushed crude back above $100 per barrel last week, with higher prices of benefit to sellers. Conversely, market volatility makes it harder for buyers and sellers to agree on valuations, as buyers want to avoid the perception of paying an inflated price. Dealmaking involving US production assets has [USN:L6N44211N TEXT:"slumped in recent months"] as a result. This uncertainty is reflected in potential valuations for Devon's Eagle Ford. The TPH Research analysts marked it at $4.5 billion, but the sources pointed to a range between $3.5 billion and roughly $4 billion. Devon is also facing pressure from activist shareholders [USN:L6N42O1EL TEXT:"TOMS Capital"] and [USN:L4N41B1LQ TEXT:"Kimmeridge Energy Management"] to improve performance and shed assets.

WASHINGTON, Sept 24 : The White House has asked OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models from British testers until a US review, Politico reported on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter and a senior US administration official. The White House wants to take steps to make sure US systems are secure before the models are shared with partners, according to the report. The White House, Anthropic and OpenAI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The development comes as the White House weighs cybersecurity risks posed by increasingly capable AI models, following a series of incidents in which AI systems gained unauthorized access to real-world computer systems.

item.title: New US sanctions shut down Iranian flights
item.description: The US sanctions aim to stop Iranian airlines from flying worldwide, while Iran warned this could increase tensions in the region.
item.dc:creator: CNA

World

New US sanctions shut down Iranian flights

The US sanctions aim to stop Iranian airlines from flying worldwide, while Iran warned this could increase tensions in the region.

Flags are held by Iranian Americans and supporters of the National Council of Resistance of Iran during a march near the US Capitol in Washington, DC, US, May 16, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Ken Cedeno)

25 Sep 2026 01:38AM

FAST

DUBAI: Iranian airlines were barred from neighbouring countries including the UAE and Oman on Thurs day (Sep 24) in response to new US sanctions , the first big impact of a shift in US policy to target companies in third countries that do business with Iran. The General Civil Aviation Authority of the United Arab Emirates, the Middle East's biggest travel hub, said that as a result of the new US policy it was suspending all flights by Iranian airlines until further notice. Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that flights had also been shut down to Oman, Georgia and Azerbaijan, and to the Iraqi capital Baghdad. It said authorities were working to route flights to another Iraqi airport, in Najaf, a major Shi'ite Muslim religious pilgrimage site. Washington had announced it would put sanctions on any global companies doing business with Iranian airlines after Sep 23, with the aim of grounding Iran's entire civil fleet worldwide.

Other countries in the Gulf region also appeared to have restricted flights. Tehran's Imam Khomeini Airport listed scheduled arrivals and departures on Thurs day to and from countries including Afghanistan, Armenia, China, Iraq, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Türkiye. But no flights appeared to be listed to or from the nearby Gulf states, with which Iran has long had some of its most important business and travel ties. Iran has suggested that enforcement of a US-mandated air blockade would lead to potential escalation. On Wednes day , a senior Iranian official threatened to make airports "unusable" in any regional country that abides by the US ban. Separately on Thurs day , authorities in Saudi Arabia said they had intercepted intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen's Houthi fighters. The Houthis said they had fired dozens of missiles and drones at Saudi targets. An escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has emerged this month as the combat zone in the wider Middle East war.

"ECONOMIC D- DAY" With the US-Israeli war against Iran largely stalemated for months on the battlefield, Washington has announced a shift in tactics to extend the reach of its financial sanctions by targeting companies from third countries that do business with Iranian firms, a practice known as "secondary sanctions". Trump referred to the new strategy last month as "economic D- Day ", comparing it to the assault on Nazi-controlled France in World War Two by the United States and its allies. A flight ban, if sustained, could deepen Iran's isolation and worsen an economic crisis in the country, which is already facing a US blockade of its ports at sea. "We are living in an open-air prison," a retired teacher in Tehran told Reuters by text message on condition her name not be used.

SAUDI ARABIA SAYS IT SHOOTS DOWN HOUTHI MISSILES The war, which Trump launched alongside Israel in February as "Operation Epic Fury", has disrupted global energy supplies, killed thousands of people and pushed up oil prices. Conflicts have been reignited in other regional countries where Iran has allies, initially in Lebanon and now in Yemen, where the Houthis declared a blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and launched a lightning advance this month against a Saudi-backed government. The Houthis have repeatedly fired into Saudi Arabia this month, and say the Saudi air force has conducted hundreds of strikes on Yemen since fighting escalated. Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles on Thurs day , after issuing emergency alerts for areas including the holy city of Mecca, Jeddah and Yanbu, the main Saudi Red Sea oil port. "Any escalation and violations by the terrorist Houthi militia will be dealt with firmly," a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen said in a statement. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had attacked Saudi military sites in Jazan province bordering Yemen, targeting operations rooms, command and control centres, weapons depots, missile launch sites and military camps.

Related:

Iran threatens to expand war to Indian Ocean if US attacks again

Iranian president says he will not allow Strait of Hormuz to be used as leverage

Sources in the internationally recognised, Saudi-backed Yemeni government said their forces had repelled overnight Houthi attacks on a key supply route to Aden, the Indian Ocean port city where the government is based. The Houthis, who already controlled the north including the capital Sanaa, seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast this month and have been pushing into adjacent highlands near the central mountain city of Taiz and the road from Aden. The Houthis have kept up pressure on government forces holding a steep winding mountain pass known as Hejat al-Abd, a lifeline for hemmed in pro-government forces, and for goods entering Taiz. Seizing parts of the Taiz-Aden road could allow the Houthis to tighten their grip around Taiz and deal another blow to the government, which has struggled to regain the initiative since losing the western coast. More than 700 people have been killed and thousands wounded in the latest fighting, according to the United Nations. Nearly 130,000 Yemenis have been displaced within the country, while more than 3,000 have fled by boat across the Red Sea to Africa.

Source: Reuters/fs

Beset by far-right rival, Italy’s Meloni tightens foreign pupil rules

Reuters

24 September, 2026 11:00 pm IST

By Angelo Amante ROME, Sept 24 (Reuters) – Italy’s right-wing government on Thursday passed rules to limit the number of foreign pupils at school and ban face coverings, a move opponents said was designed to counter the growing appeal of a rival far-right party ahead of elections due next year.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is grappling with the rise of National Future, a party founded in February by former army general Roberto Vannacci and already polling at around 8%, while surveys show her coalition trailing the centre-left bloc.

National Future has made schools a central battleground in its campaign advocating “remigration” – the deportation of foreigners to their countries of origin – and has argued that Islamic “contamination” in classrooms harms national identity.

Show Full Article

From the 2027-28 school year, a 30% cap will apply in primary school classrooms to pupils who are not Italian nationals and were not born in Italy, or who have attended fewer than two years of nursery school in the country, according to a draft decree.

The decree also imposes fines of up to €1,000 ($1,137) on anyone entering school premises wearing face coverings, which members of the ruling coalition describe as symbols of Islamist oppression and a lack of respect for women’s dignity.

“These are common-sense measures that do not divide people, but help foster genuine integration,” Meloni posted on X after cabinet approved the measures.

ITALIAN COURSES FOR PARENTS

She first unveiled the plans on Sunday at a rally of the youth wing of her Brothers of Italy party, where she also said parents of children who do not speak Italian would be required to attend language courses.

In what appeared to be a part of a broader push to rally support for the coalition ahead of a 2027 election, Meloni last week also announced a partial rollback of the unpopular road tax.

The schools measures have sparked concern among principals, who say they will be difficult to enforce in areas with large immigrant populations, particularly in northern Italy.

If demand exceeds the 30% cap, education authorities will have to redistribute pupils among nearby schools, taking into account family needs and access to education, the draft said, without specifying how that would be done in practice.

President Sergio Mattarella, who has to sign off on the decree, flagged this week that he is wary of any barriers being placed on education.

According to think tank ISMU Foundation, around 900,000 foreign students attend Italian schools, accounting for 11.6% of the total student population. About 43% come from other European countries, while 32% have African backgrounds.

Opposition politicians accused Meloni of prioritising culture-war politics over the interests of students and schools.

“It is a shameful decree that seeks to hide the government’s inability to address the real problems of the public school system behind a new ideological banner,” said Elly Schlein, the leader of the centre-left Democratic Party.

Immigration is politically sensitive in Italy, but the share of immigrants in the population remains lower than in several European peers, standing at about 12% in 2025, compared with 21% in Germany and 19% in Spain, Rockwool Foundation data shows.

($1 = 0.8793 euros)

(Reporting by Angelo Amante; Graphics by Anna Uras; Editing by Crispian Balmer and Gavin Jones)
